News.title: Traitors star burgled after sharing holiday photos
News.content:
Traitors star Paul Gorton did not think twice about sharing photographs on social media while enjoying a family holiday with his wife and two young children.

But when he returned home he discovered that his house in Cheshire had been burgled just days earlier.

"The eerie bit is at 21:10 BST I posted that me and Kate were by the side of the pool, we've got full bellies, the kids are in bed, we're actually having our little bit of the holiday," he said.

"About 20 minutes later, little did we know, our house has been broken into."

Paul's bike as well as several sentimental items including an irreplaceable ring from Kate's grandmother were stolen in the burglary on 28 August.

The perpetrators managed to break in through the bi-fold doors at the back of the house by using a technique known as lock snapping before cutting the broadband connection.

Taylor Swift has unveiled the music video for her new song “Patient Zero,” part of her extended album The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore, with an unexpected dark twist at the end.

The video, premiered at the MTV Music Video Awards Sunday after Swift accepted the inaugural Artist Director Honor, depicts 50 Shades of Grey actor Dakota Johnson as the latest woman scorned by a seemingly perfect man, played by The Penguin star Colin Farrell.

In the video, it emerges that Swift’s character is the man’s ex, who’s come back as a ghost to warn Johnson’s character that he is actually dangerous.

Throughout the video, Johnson and Swift wear the same outfits and live parallel lives, and the singer watches close by while Johnson struggles in the relationship. The video cuts to flashbacks of Swift being harmed by Farrell’s character, and him adding poison to her drink.

The music video ends with Johnson looking at a grave that’s revealed to belong to Swift’s character. The actor leaves a rose atop the gravestone for the woman.

Taylor Swift unveiled the music video for her new single ‘Patient Zero’ at the MTV Music Video Awards Sunday, after accepting the inaugural Artist Director Honor, ( AP )

“Patient Zero” tells the story of a woman reflecting on her relationship with a toxic ex, and Swift is the “patient zero” in the scenario.

The broad term patient zero typically refers to the first individual identified with a disease or an illness in a new outbreak.

In the song, Swift describes a man who “burst into your life like fireworks” before revealing his true colors. She describes that the man had “the devil on his shoulder under his halo” and that he used her for social climbing.

She then addresses Johnson’s character, singing: “It’s not for me to tell someone else what to do / But if you’re sick of him / I got you / I was patient zero.”

“I know it seems like he shines so bright / But he's bathing in your reflected light / On a free solo social climb,” she sings, also alluding to infidelity: “And when you saw another woman coming out of his place / I bet he kissed the rain off your face.”

At the MTV Video Music Awards on Sunday night, Swift accepted the first Artist Director Honors, establishing her as the most decorated performer in the event's history. Swift is currently tied with Beyoncé for the most wins at the VMAs overall, with 30 trophies each, while Eminem holds the male record with 15. The new prize raises her total to 31.

It comes after Swift released four new songs earlier this week as part of her extended album. Additional songs include “Cleveland!,” “Pink Clouding” and “Babylon.”

The release has been subject to mixed reviews from both fans and critics, with “Patient Zero” emerging as a strong favorite across the board.

The Independent’s music editor Roisin O’Connor gave the release two stars, writing that “Patient Zero” was a “diamond” track, while the rest were “duds.”

“Swift’s relentless output of late should suggest she’s on one hell of a creative streak, but the returns in the past few years have dwindled,” wrote O’Connor.

Malaysia is pushing to take durian, whose powerful smell delights its lovers and repels its haters, beyond its roadside stalls and family orchards to convince fans of the spiky fruit that its varieties are worth seeking out.

Devotees savor durians like wine. For Malaysian ones, the taste of their rich and creamy flesh varies widely across types. Some are prized for their sweet custard and fruity notes, others for a hint of bitterness, an alcohol tinge or even a peanut butter flavor.

Malaysians' efforts to elevate the industry can be found in the capital, Kuala Lumpur, at a center devoted exclusively to the fruit and the growing variety of products made from it.

At the Kuala Lumpur Durian Experience Centre, near the landmark Petronas Twin Towers, visitors venture into a replica durian orchard to discover the fruit’s culture and history. In another room, a theater show draws laughter. Downstairs, visitors enjoy platters and egg tarts crafted from it.

Launched this summer after an investment of nearly $2 million, the two-story center spans about 1,900 square meters (20,450 square feet) and is open daily. Its durian shop welcomes guests from morning to midnight.

Its founder, Edison Ang, said the center targets both local customers and tourists, especially those from China, the world's biggest durian importer. He said Chinese palates have long been influenced by Thai durian culture.

“What we actually hope for now is not to get people who don’t eat durian to start eating durian," he said. “Instead, we hope consumers who are already eating durian from other countries will switch to Malaysian durian.”

Rising demand presents challenges

In 2025, China imported 1.87 million tonnes of fresh durian worth $7.5 billion, with volume jumping over six times in the past decade, according to its customs data.

Thailand’s earlier entry helped it secure over half that market by value in 2025. Malaysia, which began exporting fresh durian to China in 2024, was dwarfed. But for the first half of 2026, the value of China's fresh durian imports from Malaysia quadrupled compared with the same period last year, pointing to rapid growth.

Unlike their rivals, Malaysian growers typically do not harvest early, instead collecting only naturally ripened fruit caught in nets or ropes as they fall.

That’s the industry’s biggest advantage and also its biggest weakness, Ang said, as sellers have to race against time because the fruit’s shelf life is at most two to three days. Any delays would affect its quality. When his stock got held up for several days during customs checks, his refund rate climbed, he said.

Durian sales are also sensitive to economic conditions, said Leron Yee, founder of DKing, whose business covers both export and domestic markets. When the Chinese economy performs well, his business improves, but if the buying power of Chinese consumers falls, he needs to find alternative markets, he said.

“It is a luxury, not a necessity,” he said.

Going beyond the fruit itself

Businesses are finding opportunities in what the fruit can become. Yee's business sells durian paste, durian-flavored chocolate and mochi — and even mooncakes ahead of the Mid-Autumn Festival.

DurianBB founder Adrian Choy's company offers durian ice cream, desserts and dried durian at a cafe, alongside coffee flavored with the Musang King variety and other items. His brand also offers guided farm tours.

In July, Choy's brand went a step further and launched a durian flower perfume that smells sweet and floral.

Choy said branching into other products is important because it will add value to the food itself and differentiate his business, even when others compete on price.

“Food is food,” he said. “You cannot sell it like 50% more because your branding is different."

Tasting it in Malaysia

Across China, durian specialty shops have mushroomed, with some specializing in Malaysian varieties. In Beijing, the Jiang Sir durian shop sells platters priced roughly between 300 and 1,000 yuan (about $44 to $150), depending on the weight of the pulp and the varieties chosen.

Its employee, Hou Yuxin, welcomed the growing number of similar shops and brushed off pressure from competition, saying it would help boost the market for Malaysian durians. She noted many people now want to enjoy durians during their trips to Malaysia.

Back at Ang’s center in Kuala Lumpur, Henry Zhang was one of them. Zhang, a visitor from Shanghai who started eating durian during his university days, saw a durian no bigger than his palm for the first time.

He said Malaysian ones were creamier than those from Thailand and had different flavors. He was impressed by the center offering more than just the fruit.

“I may still eat durians from other countries. But after eating them, I may miss Malaysian ones even more,” Zhang said.

___

Associated Press photographer Vincent Thian and video journalists Olivia Zhang and Wu Jia in Beijing contributed to this report.

Winners of the 2026 MTV Music Video Awards have been announced, recognizing excellence in pop culture, music and video production.

This year’s awards show is hosted by Snoop Dogg at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, California.

Nominations are dominated this year by Madonna, Taylor Swift, Ariana Grande and Sabrina Carpenter.

Madonna is the artist with the most nominations, with 11 nods, including best artist, song of the year and best collaboration, for works from her latest album Confessions II. To date, she holds 19 competitive VMA trophies and was recognized in 1986 as the inaugural solo female recipient of the Video Vanguard Award.

So far at the ceremony, Lisa & Kentara Sakaguchi beat out Swift, Charli xcx, Grande, Olivia Rodrigo, Carpenter and Tate McRae in the Best Pop category, with the song “Dream.”

Elsewhere at the ceremony, Swift accepted the first Artist Director Honors, establishing her as the most decorated performer in the event's history. Swift is currently tied with Beyoncé for the most wins at the VMAs overall, with 30 trophies each, while Eminem holds the male record with 15. The new prize will raise her total to 31.

Meanwhile, singers Raye, Sombr and Teddy Swims will perform a tribute to the late George Michael. Other performers include GENER8ION with Yung Lean, Shaboozey with Gunna as well as Lisa, Raye and Sienna Spiro.

A former Cornell University student is suing the college and seven male fraternity members, alleging she was drugged and gang-raped for hours in a brutal attack, and that the university failed to protect her or adequately punish those responsible.

In a 101-page civil complaint, filed September 14 in New York County Supreme Court, the plaintiff, identified as Jane Doe, alleges the assault occurred in October 2024 at Cornell’s Chi Phi fraternity house in Ithaca, New York.

According to the documents, obtained by The Independent, Jane Doe was 20 years old at the time and a member of a campus sorority. The suit alleges she was visiting a friend at the house and was intoxicated when two male students pressured her into snorting a substance they claimed was ketamine.

The lawsuit states that after an initial sexual assault, one of the men sent a message to the fraternity’s active Snapchat group chat stating there was “free p****” and inviting additional members to join. Multiple male students later arrived, and Doe was subjected to an hours-long assault by seven of them, according to the complaint.

The filing details graphic abuse including men snorting lines of ketamine off her body, moving her between rooms, and continuing to rape and sexually assault her while she was incapacitated, before she finally lost consciousness around 5:45 a.m.

open image in gallery Jane Doe is suing the Ivy League college and seven male students, alleging she was drugged and gang-raped inside a fraternity house during an hours-long assault that university officials failed to prevent or adequately punish ( Getty Images )

The lawsuit identifies the alleged perpetrators and the national and local sorority chapter. It also names two local bars, and several university-affiliated individuals as co-defendants for their alleged roles in failing to monitor, supervise or protect the plaintiff.

As the exchange unfolded in the Snapchat thread, one of the accused members allegedly sent a message celebrating the encounter, writing: “I f****** love chi phi.”

Doe reported the incident to the Cornell University Police Department approximately three weeks later on November 8, 2024. An internal Title IX investigation was launched in January 2025, and at least 12 hearings followed. But Doe’s attorney Thomas Giuffra said that the university’s response was severely lacking.

Giuffra told The Independent that graduating from Cornell was his client’s dream from childhood after years of hard work.

“Her dreams were destroyed by a group of men who sought to abuse and humiliate her,” Giuffra said. “She was subjected to unspeakable horrors that I have not seen in my 30 years of handling abuse cases.”

He pointed to the fraternity’s group chat messages as evidence of their cruelty.

“The arrogance and cruelty of these men was demonstrated in the fraternity group message which went to every single member of the fraternity inviting them to rape Ms. Doe,” Giuffra said. “It is truly disheartening that nobody tried to help her and instead laughing comments were made. The lack of humanity displayed was surprising for a group of men who are supposed to be the best and brightest.”

Of the seven male students named in the civil filing, only two were ultimately expelled by Cornell, according to Doe’s legal team. The remaining students received lesser administrative sanctions, such as temporary suspensions, required workshops or essay-writing assignments.

Court filings show that around November 8, 2024, temporary suspensions were issued for several male students who “were afforded the opportunity to mitigate their conduct by submitting essays to CORNELL.”

Giuffra cited failures by law enforcement, explaining that Doe never received a call back from the Cornell Police Department after filing her initial report.

“Based on the group chat evidence, it was obvious that the complaint warranted an investigation and criminal charges against the involved abusers,” Giuffra told The Independent. “Instead Ms. Doe heard nothing.”

The Tompkins County District Attorney’s Office stated that after conducting “a thorough review of the police investigation,” officials determined “there was insufficient evidence to support criminal charges.”

The lawsuit has drawn intense criticism toward the university’s handling of sexual misconduct cases, particularly given prior police responses to drug-related incidents reported at the fraternity house shortly before the alleged assault.

In an editorial published by The Cornell Daily Sun, the student newspaper’s editorial board condemned the administration’s response, questioning why students accused of severe misconduct were allowed to write essays as part of their discipline.

open image in gallery Cornell University expelled two students following a Title IX probe into the alleged sexual assault but new civil court filings reveal others were permitted to write essays to mitigate their discipline. That response was condemned by the campus newspaper as ‘belittling’ ( Getty Images )

“Tackling sexual assault as an academic matter — complete with its charts and facts and figures — offers no respite to the victims who have undergone physical and mental abuse,” The Sun wrote. “Academic ‘solutions,’ like the essays, allegedly offered to the defendants to mitigate their suspensions, is belittling to the severity of the crime.”

The editorial board also pointed to institutional delays and transparency failures, noting that a task force convened by the university months after the incident did little to address systemic risks.

“Only those who perpetrate sexual violence benefit from its concealment,” The Sun quoted from a November 2024 university letter, adding that “Cornell has failed to protect its students.”

In a September 21 statement, Cornell University defended its administrative procedures and cited federal privacy laws regarding student records.

“The Cornell Office of Civil Rights and the Office of Student Conduct and Community Standards investigated and adjudicated the allegations consistent with university policies,” the university said. “The Xi chapter of Chi Phi fraternity remains barred from our campus. Federal privacy law prohibits Cornell from disclosing specific information regarding individual students and we therefore are unable to make a public statement on any other disciplinary response.

“Violations of university policies could lead to sanctions up to and including suspension or expulsion. We will respond in detail through the legal process.”

The national headquarters of Chi Phi also addressed the lawsuit in a statement to CBS News, calling the allegations “deeply concerning.”

“Chi Phi unequivocally condemns sexual violence,” the organization said. “Our founding principles of Truth, Honor, and Personal Integrity, and our mission of Building Better Men, call on every brother to demonstrate character through his actions and respect for the dignity and safety of others. Sexual violence is fundamentally incompatible with those expectations.

“We are aware of the lawsuit concerning an alleged incident in 2024. While we cannot discuss the specific allegations during pending litigation, we take this matter seriously.”

Doe, who dropped out of the university following the incident, is seeking unspecified compensatory and punitive monetary damages, alleging breach of contract, negligence, negligent supervision, premises liability and state law violations.

Giuffra said that although Doe voluntarily participated in the university’s Title IX investigation, the institution's response left her with no alternative.

“The anemic response led her to conclude that the only avenue for justice was to file a lawsuit against the involved parties,” Giuffra said.

Following the filing of the lawsuit, an employer associated with one of the accused students addressed the allegations on social media on September 27, stating they were aware of the situation, actively reviewing his status and investigating whether any company standards were violated.

The Independent has contacted Cornell University for further comment.

For those affected by rape and sexual abuse, if you are in the United States, you can call Rainn on 800-656-HOPE (4673).

Rape Crisis also offers support.You can call them on 0808 802 9999 in England and Wales, 0808 801 0302 in Scotland, and 0800 0246 991 in Northern Ireland, or visit their website at www.rapecrisis.org.uk.

White House Deputy Chief of Staff Dan Scavino is facing fierce backlash — even from fellow Republicans — over a social media post depicting him in a tuxedo, sloshing champagne with some glamorous party pals as Americans grapple with a deepening cost-of-living crisis linked to the Iran War and the Trump administration’s tariffs.

Scavino shared the apparent AI-generated video depicting him and who appears to be his second wife, Erin Elmore, and Lara Trump, grinning in ballgowns while they are pushed on a gold luggage cart through the White House by Eric Trump to Pitbull’s “Don’t Stop the Party.” Gold confetti falls before a jubilant President Donald Trump enters the scene.

“This is not an intended for the Dems heads to explode — Being some of the post State Dinner party has gotten out, I felt inclined to share mine as well, in complete transparency, with the American People. GOD BLESS THE USA!!!” Scavino, 50, posted.

However, it wasn’t just Democrats who had a knee-jerk reaction to the post, which comes as Trump’s poll numbers continue to plummet ahead of the November midterms.

“You really have no shame, do you? Many Americans can’t afford groceries, gas or their mortgage payment, and you post a tone deaf AI video of you and your buddies partying at the People’s House,” conservative activist Carrie Prejean Boller wrote.

open image in gallery An apparent AI-generated video by White House Deputy Chief of Staff Dan Scavino showed him partying and spraying champagne with some glamorous companions ( Dan Scavino/X )

“One of my friends couldn’t afford air conditioner this summer,” Meghan McCain, conservative commentator and daughter of late Republican Senator John McCain, commented on the video.

Jonah Goldberg, editor-in-chief of center-right publication The Dispatch, quipped: “This is precisely the midterm messaging the GOP needs from the Deputy White House Chief of Staff.”

Sarah Longwell, an anti-Trump Republican who founded the Bulwark, called it “Real fall of Rome s***.”

Other self-described MAGA accounts on X also slammed the video. One X user wrote: “Wow... This is really going to resonate with everyday Americans. They are so out of touch. It's astonishing.”

“Very relatable to Americans who are getting crushed by inflation, gas prices & cost of living,” another noted.

CNN anchor Jake Tapper also reshared the post, simply noting: “WH deputy chief of staff.”

open image in gallery Scavino, the White House’s deputy chief of staff, later shared another AI-generated video showing Trump and other White House officials partying at the White House with Chinese President Xi Jinping after the State Dinner ( AFP/Getty )

Scavino appeared to lean into the controversy by resharing another AI-generated video that showed a rowdy party after the State Dinner at the White House. The images depict Trump, Elon Musk, Marco Rubio and other officials partying with Chinese President Xi Jinping. Scavino wrote “...as the typical nutters are losing their s*** over AI created content, well done! It is AI, correct?”

The Independent has contacted the White House for comment.

There is little over a month to go until the midterm elections. New polling from NBC News shows Democrats with a 9-point advantage over Republicans when it comes to taking control of Congress. Decision Desk HQ forecasts a 72 percent probability of Democrats taking control of the House and a 54 percent probability of the party winning the Senate.

President Donald Trump is facing the worst approval rating of his second term at just 32 percent, according to Reuters.

open image in gallery China's President Xi Jinping and President Donald Trump speak through interpreters while First Lady Melania Trump talks with Tesla CEO Elon Musk at a State Dinner in Washington, D.C. last week ( AFP/Getty )

Trump campaigned in 2024 on lowering costs for everyday Americans and not starting any new wars but the U.S. conflict with Iran has led to elevated prices at gas pump, grocery store and across a plethora of everyday essentials.

The president has undertaken a number of taxpayer-funded lavish renovations at the White House including breaking ground on a $600 million ballroom.

A recent Politico poll showed 53 percent of Americans couldn’t recall struggling harder to make ends meet — and 46 percent said they felt that Trump was fully or mostly responsible for the state of the economy.

Democrats have hammered Republicans by campaigning on the cost of living crisis ahead of the November midterms - and at least some in the Republican party have taken note.

Senator Jim Justice, a West Virginia Republican, openly criticized his party’s current approach.

“You’ve got Republicans scrambling everywhere,” Justice told The New York Post this week. “When — my lord of living, all we had to do was really be in touch with the people four or five months ago … We’ve done all kinds of great stuff. You know, but we’re tone deaf in a lot of ways.”

News.title: Five reasons why Australia’s win over Boks was an all-time classic
News.content:
If the Wallabies play like this in their own backyard at their own World Cup next year, boy we are in for a treat. After years in the doldrums, this five-try victory over South Africa was the latest reminder of their transformation under the stewardship of Les Kiss.

Their gritty performance in Perth – the city where Australia will open rugby’s showpiece in 12 months’ time – was caveated by the fact they were facing a second-string Boks side. But there can be no denying they are on an upward trajectory, even if their discipline dramatically deserted them late on.

In a helter-skelter denouement, Australia played the majority of the final 10 minutes of the match with 11 men on the pitch as South Africa threatened to mount a late comeback. Tom Wright’s eye-catching intercept try looked to have secured a match-winning moment, but it was scratched off after Hunter Paisami joined Harry Wilson, Ryan Lonergan and Joseph Sua’ali’i in the bin.

Ox Nche’s 80th-minute score made it a four-point game with time left for the restart, but Australia had enough fight to secure a dramatic victory largely built on execution and patience.

Five tries by the hour mark, including a Len Ikitau first-half double, ultimately gave South Africa a mountain to climb. The Wallabies’ field coverage and industriousness in defence was far superior to that of the four-time world champions, while Max Jorgensen and Sua’ali’i were pillars of excellence out wide.

After clinching a 3-1 win over New Zealand in their historic “Greatest Rivalry” series, Rassie Erasmus had the luxury of resting several of his A-listers for this one-off Test in Western Australia. The changes ultimately had an adverse effect, with the visitors faulty at the set-piece and lacking their usual snarl and bite. They found themselves playing catch-up in a chaotic game that Australia, despite their discipline creaking in the dying moments, deserved to win.

Here, Telegraph Sport explores five reasons why this was one of the craziest Test matches in recent memory.

Wallabies outmuscle Boks over 60 emphatic minutes

The Wallabies front up impressively to earn a seven-point lead at the break after a quickfire Len Ikitau double cancels out tries from Johan Grobbelaar and Edwill van der Merwe, before Ben Donaldson finishes a sublime attacking set from the hosts.

News.title: England show ODI depth in thrashing of Sri Lanka
News.content:
England’s international summer comes to an end at the Oval with a series decider against Sri Lanka. After England won the first game in Durham, Sri Lanka bounced back to take a 16-run win at Headingley on Thursday to set up this winner-takes-all match today. Sri Lanka put up a much better fight in the second one-day international than they have throughout the rest of their white-ball tour. The tourists posted 321 for six, with their captain Kusal Mendis leading the way with 121 off 100 balls, his seventh ODI century.

England’s reply got off to the best possible start, with both openers Tom Banton and Ben Duckett hitting fifties. It appeared to be going well for England, with Jos Buttler and Will Jacks also registering half centuries, but Buttler’s hamstring injury in addition to the regular loss of wickets meant Sri Lanka were able to claim victory to take us to a series decider in London today.

“I am so happy winning and getting the hundred,” Mendis said. “The overall performance was very good. We started really well and the middle order batted really well. Nothing special, basic cricket and I was very happy with 320, we wanted more than 300 on this pitch. [Dunith] Wellalage bowled really well, the whole team, after the powerplay. The guys gave 100 per cent. Today [Thursday] is finished and now we have to focus on the next game and do the basics right.”

When Buttler retired hurt in the 38th over of England’s run chase, the hosts were 254 for four and were in a great position to chase the total down and claim a series victory. From the 37th over onwards, England were only able to score one four and one six.

“It was an outstanding game,” England captain Harry Brook said. “You can look back and dwell on some many different areas but that is not what this team does, we go back to the drawing board and get ready for the Oval. We put up a really good fight with the ball. To restrict them to 320 and have the chance to chase that down was a hell of an effort.

“The lads got the chase off to a flyer. You could not really ask for much more. We probably stalled in that middle period and lost a few too many wickets, but the fight we showed was great. We have got a great opportunity now to try and win this series, and a great opportunity for 12 months’ time. In pressure situations, like the one that awaits us at the Oval, it will be great to see where we are as a team.”

Buttler has been ruled out of this match due to a hamstring injury and has been replaced in the squad by Dan Lawrence, who had been playing for Surrey in the final round of the County Championship.

Play from the Oval will get under way at 10.30am.

News.title: Saracens storm Leicester to launch new Venter era in style
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Gallagher Prem meeting as Leicester Tigers host Saracens at Welford Road.

Last season, Leicester reached the play-off semi-finals in Geoff Parling’s first full season at the club, before losing to arch-rivals Northampton Saints, who went on to win their third title in the competition.

In a new era for Leicester as they plot a route back to the very top, Aaron Wainwright and Mako Vunipola make their Prem debuts.

Leicester head coach Geoff Parling is brimming with excitement ahead of this tasty match and has talked about his side’s preparation for the new season.

“Firstly we are looking to evolve our game, we’re not looking to rip it up and completely restart,” he said. This team is built on being competitive and winning, we’ve got to be in the mix every year. For me it’s all about being consistently near the top and then getting in those big games and having the ability to perform in them.”

“I’m well aware that there’s lots of elements from the season and different circumstances but the main thing is that the league is designed to have a top four that go into the play-offs so the top four is the aim.”

Saracens finished one place below Leicester in the previous campaign and missed out on the play-offs after a 32-12 final round loss to Exeter Chiefs.

Boss Joe Shaw has handed debuts to Tomos Williams and Alfie Barbeary, and he’s raring to go ahead of this fixture.

“We’ve had a great pre-season, but we’re itching to get stuck into the league campaign now,” he said. “We have a really competitive squad who are driving standards and good habits across the pitch. We are confident in the squad we have put together and are excited to see what they can achieve this campaign.”

Kick-off is at 15:00.

News.title: England throw it away with defending unworthy of a top nation
News.content:
Tuchel does not plan to address the issue with his players ahead of the remaining Nations League games against Czech Republic and Croatia.

Asked if the City verdict had been a cause of discussion ahead of the Spain game, Tuchel replied: “Not for me, but I can imagine maybe for the Man City players. I won’t comment on it as it’s an ongoing case.

“I didn’t make it a topic. It was not a topic for me. I’m just thinking about Spain and the team and meetings. The players have more time than me. So I can imagine they talk about it. It’s good they do. I don’t think it was a distraction for them.”

Kane added: “There was a discussion, but when we’re with England, we kind of put club football to one side and it was no different this week.”

Tuchel also refused to point the finger of blame at Guéhi, O’Reilly or Kane, who missed a penalty, for England’s defeat despite admitting his team got off to the worst possible start by conceding a goal after two minutes.

“We will focus on the positives, but also highlight the stuff we can do better,” Tuchel said. “Not even speaking about individual mistakes because this is normal. It just happens. It should not happen, and for sure not in this amount. But there is no sense in showing the individual mistakes or telling them ‘please don’t make mistakes’. That is normal, but we can do things better. We can defend the third goal better. But we will focus on the positives. There is a lot to take away from the game.

“We wanted to be the team desperately to beat them [Spain] and we think we had them. We still think we had them at half-time. That was the way the team showed up after half-time. So we will focus on that, but the reality is we lost and the reality is we need to prove it again.”

News.title: Red Roses triumph over New Zealand in chaotic late scenes – how it unfolded
News.content:
Just when it looked like the Red Roses’ lustre was beginning to fade, up stepped Zoe Harrison.

In one of the most dramatic finishes to an England match in recent memory, the fly-half gobbled up Amy Du Plessis’s pass to glide over the whitewash and secure a pulsating win over New Zealand.

Ever the epitome of calmness, Harrison was undeterred by the fact she had just missed what would have been a match-winning penalty from 42 metres out with the score locked at 19-19.

But after their arm-wrestle with Canada last weekend in Exeter, which finished 26-26, there was simply no way the Red Roses were going to settle for a draw for a second week running.

A year to the day since they were crowned world champions in their own back yard, England’s status as the most dominant side in the women’s game was all but confirmed by this never-say-die victory over the Black Ferns.

News.title: Russell holds his nerve to see off Verstappen and win Azerbaijan GP
News.content:
The Azerbaijan Grand Prix weekend went the way many believed the 2026 season would play out. George Russell strolled to victory from pole, though with a little late jeopardy, whilst Kimi Antonelli’s crash in qualifying meant he had to fight his way through the field to finish fifth. That, after all, was the order of things last season.

Yet the past few days in Baku are an inversion of the season’s storyline. It is Antonelli who has been the faster driver, heading for a maiden world title at the second time of asking. Russell has been the troubled one. This was only the Briton’s third victory of the season and his first since Austria in late June. Antonelli has racked up eight wins and, before this weekend in Baku, a well-deserved 81-point lead over Russell.

Russell’s dominant and impressive run from pole to the chequered flag on Saturday is both a reminder of what he is capable of and also what might have been, had he been able to find this type of form earlier and more often. The reality, though, is that he needs to replicate this for the rest of the season to even be in with a sniff, barring a catastrophic meltdown from Antonelli. Still, Russell looked elated to have ended his barren run.

The finish was a little more tense than Russell deserved, having established a healthy lead in the first half of the race. Two late safety cars eradicated his advantage and helped put Max Verstappen’s Red Bull on his gearbox. In the end, he triumphed by just under 0.2sec and, as Antonelli finished fifth – with some help from two safety-car inducing crashes – he made up 15 points on his Mercedes team-mate. Isack Hadjar completed the podium for Red Bull after missing the past three races with a wrist injury.

News.title: Scotland’s Pocognoli era starts with encouraging signs but familiar issues in front of goal
News.content:
Scotland’s ramped-up second-half performance offered some cause for optimism as Sébastien Pocognoli’s tenure as head coach began with a goalless draw with Slovenia in Ljubljana.

The 39-year-old Belgian head coach, appointed in August as Steve Clarke’s successor, refreshed the side for the Nations League Group B1 opener in the Stozice Stadium, but they were fortunate on a couple of occasions at least not to fall behind before rallying before the break.

Scotland had been insipid and uninspiring for most of the first half but after the interval they played with pace and purpose as Slovenia captain and goalkeeper Jan Oblak became a key figure, making saves from Oli McBurnie and Kieron Bowie.

News.title: Carreras’ try-of-season contender helps Bath eclipse Harlequins
News.content:
And they kept playing, it was not until Richards scored in the 72nd minute that the game was decided. Still for Bath, a five-try victory away from home, felt like a decent return.

If they were to stand any chance of finding a way back into the game, Quins had to score first after the restart. They were rewarded for their attacking intent after running from a scrum deep in their half, with Murley cutting a brilliant line before Pedro Delgado drove over for his side’s third try.

Quins had the opportunity to further cut the deficit when first Sam Riley carried down the left wing and Cameron Anderson drove into the Bath 22. But as Quins looked to pick and go, Beno Obano and Guy Pepper combined to hold the ball up over the line.

It felt like a significant moment and when Riley was shown a yellow card for a high tackle on Obano moments later, the odds against a Quins comeback lengthened again. Yet there was something sticky about their resilience.

“I am really happy with the grit and the fight that they showed, particularly in the second half,” said Gilmore. “We had some massive defensive sets on our goal-line which we withstood. I reckon they were the moments last year that Bath would probably run in three tries really quickly and kick the score out, which is good.”

Bath emptied their bench, including the introduction of England flanker Pepper, but they could not pull away as expected in the final quarter, despite some impressive contributions by Tom de Glanville.

It was left to their line-out maul to score their first points of the second half, with Richards touching down to seal Harlequins’ fate. Still, there were enough promising glimpses to give Harlequins supporters hope that more encouraging days lie ahead.

Sports.title: Ireland beat Israel 3-0 as players bow heads during anthem & no on-pitch handshakes amid calls for FAI board to resign
Sports.content:
Next

IRELAND’S footballers let their feet do the talking as they hammered Israel in the controversial Nations League clash.

The most contentious sporting fixture in recent memory passed off without any major incident, with the men’s senior side cruising to a 3-0 win in Hungary.



As the debate over whether the game should have gone ahead – due to the war in Gaza – continued on, Heimir Hallgrimsson’s side produced a thrilling display to bag a vital three points.

But despite the resounding result, calls were growing for the FAI board to RESIGN over its decision to fulfil their two games against Israel, with fierce opposition to the call at home.



Sinn Fein, the Social Democrats and the Green Party all said the leadership at the soccer body should consider stepping down after chaos surrounding the team in recent days.

One of the most eventful weekends in Irish sporting memory ahead of tonight’s tie saw preparations thrown into disarray over the weekend.

Keeper Gavin Bazunu’s sensational withdrawal from the squad sparked fresh discussions over whether the game would go ahead – and there are now questions over whether the second match will take place.

The Irish Sun has learned that there are major doubts over whether the return Israel tie in Backa Topola will be played, and more developments are expected this week.



Under-pressure boss Heimir Hallgrimsson admitted ahead of kick-off: “It’s been one of the most challenging weeks for me as a coach, and I guess it’s the same for most of the players, a situation we’ve not been in before.

“I feel for the players mostly. It’s our job to try and protect all of them. As you can expect, the preparation has been probably as bad as it can be.”

Asked about the strong Israel feelings at home, he admitted: “It’s tricky. It’s kind of like I’ve said before… you will always have things objected [to] from one side or the other. And it’s kind of whatever you do, there’s always going to be people that are against it.”



A small section of around 200 Israeli fans inside the 20,000 ground booed the Irish players as they took part in the warm-up.

RTE’s coverage of the fixture was delayed until 7:40pm, rather than the usual 7pm slot, as the national broadcaster offered reduced coverage.

There was no studio coverage, pundits or Irish commentary team, with viewers left with a bare-bones offering featuring an international feed.

Although Hallgrimsson spoke to the station’s Tony O’Donoghue ahead of kick-off, the Cork presenter was among the only RTE staff to be shown on TV.

Ireland’s players wore black armbands as part of their personal protests over the war in Gaza, and will donate their match fees towards charity.



The team bowed their heads as the Israeli anthem was played and there were no pre-match handshakes or exchanging of team pennants.

But the handful of Green Army foot soldiers who made into the ground were fortunate to witness a first half masterclass from the team.

Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan scored three times inside the first 25 minutes as Ireland put Israel to the sword.

Moylan marked his first competitive international goal by hoisting his armband in the air and pointing to his Ireland crest.

In the second half, Hallgrimsson’s men could have added to their tally but were worthy winners as they ended the game comfortable 3-0 winners.



There were no post-match handshakes on the pitch, and RTE’s coverage ended just seconds after the final whistle.

There were no handshakes between the benches after the referee ended things, as both teams went back into the tunnel separately, having acknowledged the handful of Irish fans in the stands.

The game itself had attracted huge global interest and Bazunu’s bombshell decision to walk away received praise from former Labour UK leader Jeremy Corbyn on Sunday.

The UK MP said: “Well done to Ireland goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu for taking the principled decision to withdraw from the game against Israel.

“He should never have been put in this position, but he has shown immense moral courage and integrity by doing the right thing in the face of genocide.”



As thoughts now turn to Thursday’s home game on Thursday, Green Party Leader Roderic O’Gorman slammed Association officials and urged them to step away as a result of the weekend’s chaos.

The TD said: “The entire FAI senior management and board need to consider their position.

“They have catastrophically mismanaged this situation from the outset.

“Rather than listen to and understand the mood of football fans, they outsourced the decision to play to the individual consciences of the players.

“It is massively unfair to put this call on the shoulders of young players at the beginning of their careers. Making players vote the day before a match only divides the team.”



Sinn Fein Dublin MEP Lynn Boylan insisted the leadership from the FAI was “completely absent”.

Boylan fumed the FAI’s approach to the Israel game had “caused a huge amount of division in the football team”.

And she rapped: “They have failed the players and failed to protect the players.”

Sinn Fein TD Joanna Byrne branded it a “dark day” for the FAI.

She added that the board, in particular its president Paul Cooke and chief executive David Courell, “must now reflect on whether they are the right people to pick up the pieces”.



Byrne declared: “The decision to ignore the will of the Irish people and fulfil the game against Israel will go down as the worst decision ever made by any board of the FAI, and that is saying something.”

Meanwhile, the Social Democrats also called for heads to roll at the FAI after a “shameful and shambolic weekend in Irish football”.

Social Democrats sports spokesperson Daniel Ennis said: “This weekend has been one of the most shameful and shambolic weekends in Irish football. With 24 hours to go before the match with Israel, our players were forced to vote on whether that game should go ahead.

“That decision, which should never have been left up to individual players, will leave a dark stain on Irish football and this country. It is at odds with the majority view of the Irish people.

“It is now clear that our players have been hung out to dry by both the FAI and the Irish government. The gross mismanagement of this whole debacle is the fault of the FAI board, who were more concerned with points in the Nations League than a live-streamed genocide being committed by Israel in Gaza. For that reason, the board must resign. I see no future for them.”



Dublin’s iconic Ha’penny Bridge was draped in Stop The Game banners, while a number of pubs opted against showing the match in solidarity.

Ireland-Palestine Solidarity Campaign (IPSC) activists unfurled massive 22-metre-long banners saying “RED CARD GENOCIDAL ISRAEL” and “IRELAND STANDS WITH PALESTINE” to coincide with the contentious match.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

IPSC Chairperson Zoë Lawlor said: “The FAI has turned down the unique opportunity to show leadership, to reflect the will of the majority of people here, of so much of the football community, and to be on the right side of history. Imagine the legacy they could have created, imagine the domino effect.”

“Instead, they have grossly mismanaged this from start to finish and passed up every opportunity to show integrity.”

Sports.title: ‘Rigged racket’ – Why Man City financial punishment is a ‘terrifying’ blow for EFL dreamers & proves ambition is dead
Sports.content:
Next

THERE are a lot of people rejoicing at the prospect of Manchester City being heavily punished for breaking Premier League financial rules.

But if you are a fan of any EFL club with aspirations of climbing the ladder, this is not a cause for celebration.



In fact, it is a terrifying reminder that ambition in English football is ultimately pointless.

The Prem’s sustainability rules are dressed up as a noble crusade to protect clubs — but let’s just stop pretending.



Aston Villa and Manchester City do not need protecting.

And while strict owner checks are vital to stop rogue cowboy owners destroying historic institutions like Bury and Macclesfield, stopping wealthy benefactors from bankrolling a dream is a disgrace.

The powers that be have built what looks like a know-your-place cartel designed to keep ambitious Championship clubs such as West Ham, Wolves, Sheffield United, Southampton, Burnley, Birmingham and even Wrexham firmly under their thumb.

What do clubs currently scrapping in the Championship have to look forward to if they win promotion?

A rigged division where you are expected to play with both hands tied behind your back.

The gap between the top flight and EFL is already a canyon, yet any promoted side trying to spend and show any sort of ambition faces sanctions.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Remember Jack Walker bankrolling Blackburn to the Premier League title in 1995? A fairytale like that would be illegal under today’s rules.

In the 34 seasons since the Premier League was formed, only two non- established heavyweights — Blackburn and Leicester — have ever broken the stranglehold of the elite to win the title.

Only seven clubs have won it.

Compare that to the 34 years prior to 1992 when the likes of Derby, Nottingham Forest, Villa, Everton, Ipswich, Leeds, Burnley, Tottenham and Wolves all were able to rise up and conquer the country.

In total, 13 clubs won the title in that same period.



There was a real chance back then for more teams to reach the pinnacle and write themselves into folklore.

Now, any football club owner who dares to dream is painted as a villain for daring to spend their own money to challenge the establishment.

And Premier League chiefs only protect the same self-interested heavyweights who tried to break away and sell out the English game with their European Super League.

What were Man City charged with? MAN CITY have been found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges they were initially hit with. Those charges were upped to 130 and fit into the following six categories… Failing to give accurate financial information over sponsorship revenue, related parties and operating costs between 2009-10 and 2017/18. Total charges: 50

Failing to provide full details of managerial remuneration between 2009/10 and 2012/13. Total charges 8

Failing to provide full details of player remuneration between 2010/11 and 2015/16. Total charges 12

Failing to comply with Uefa Licencing and Financial Fair Play regulations between 2013/14 and 2017/18. Total charges 5

Breaching Premier League Profitability and Sustainability rules between 2015/16 and 2017/18. Total charges 25

Failing to co-operate with the Premier League investigation between 2018/19 and 2022/23. Total charges 30

Total charges: 130

Football is not a level playing field — it’s a rigged racket.



Manchester City busting open that closed shop was a good thing, stopping the usual suspects from enjoying a total monopoly.

I want to see more clubs do exactly what City did because, without big spending, the so-called Big Six will just keep dominating our game forever.

Well-run clubs like Brentford, Brighton and Bournemouth — who have gone up from the Championship — deserve huge credit for their sustainable models.

But, let’s be honest, none of them will ever be allowed to replicate Brian Clough’s Forest by winning the European Cup in 1979 and 1980.

You may squeeze into the Conference League or Europa League once in a generation — but that is as far as you will ever get.



The glass ceiling has been bolted shut, sealed, and then reinforced by executives terrified of real competition.

I don’t think City being punished should be cause for celebration for anyone who loves football.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

It should just act as a bitter, painful reminder that having genuine ambition in the English game is pointless.

Punishing clubs for spending money is not fair play — it is a system engineered to keep the elite rich and the EFL’s ambitious dreamers stuck firmly in their place.

Sports.title: How Ben Watson’s 2013 FA Cup winner sparked Man City’s 13-year cheat storm with chief boasting: We can do what we want
Sports.content:
Next

BEN WATSON’S last minute winner in the 2013 FA Cup final still sends a shiver down the spines of Manchester City fans.

The shock defeat at the hands of a local rivals Wigan who were heading for relegation was bad enough and it also spelled the end of popular manager Roberto Mancini’s reign.



But is one of the most disappointing days of the Abu Dhabi era about to come back and haunt them again – 13 years on?

The Etihad giants have been found guilty of the vast majority of the charges of financial wrong-doing levelled against them by the Premier League.



And much of the top flight’s case was believed to be centred on the emails obtained by German publication Der Spiegel back in 2018.

One of the key allegations they exposed involved that infamous day at Wembley and the fall-out that followed.



Mancini was furious that stories about Manuel Pellegrini taking over from him had emerged on the morning of the final.

A couple of days after the defeat, his worst fears were realised and before long the Chilean had taken over at the helm.



Yet the cost of getting rid of the current Italy international boss also caused an issue.

It is claimed that Jorge Chumillas, the club’s chief financial officer, was compiling the financial reports for the 2012-13 season.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

He was concerned that the cost of sacking Mancini was around £9.9million – leaving them with a sizeable shortfall to meet Uefa’s financial fair play restrictions.

According to Der Spiegel, Ferran Soriano, City’s chief exec, said this problem could be overcome if the club was paid the bonus from the sponsors for winning the FA Cup.



Yet there was no bonus as Roberto Martinez and his Latics team had won the game at Wembley – thanks to Watson’s late header.

So a compromise was reached whereby various – including Etihad Airways and Aabar Investments – would have their payments adjusted and the gap would be made up.

The publication claims that Chumillas asked if it was possible to change the date of sponsorship payments.

And long-serving board member Simon Pearce – who is also an advisor to Khaldoon Al Mubarak – is alleged to have replied: ‘Of course – we can do what we want’.

The email chain was part of the evidence when Uefa found City guilty of serious breaches of their FFP rules in 2020 – and hit them with a two-year ban.



The club took their appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport and successfully got the ban overturned.

City are certain to fight the Prem’s victory too and the statement from Khaldoon on Saturday suggests they remain confident of overturning it.

Sports.title: Tuchel lucky qualifying for tournaments so easy now.. legendary back-fours have failed before and this lot are miles off

I am struggling to think of a back four as weak as the one that started against Spain — Jarrell Quansah, Ezri Konsa, Marc Guehi and Nico O’Reilly.

Even teams that failed to reach major tournaments in 1984, 1994 and 2008 had better.



Thomas Tuchel will not admit it but he must be worried about how his team defends.

World Cup winners Spain could have been 5-0 up at Wembley with England carrying on from where they left off at the tournament — they conceded 12 goals to La Roja’s one.



In fact, Tuchel’s lads have now shipped 13 in their last six games after letting in just seven in his first SEVENTEEN matches.

The German has to accept that right-back Reece James and centre-back John Stones are too injury prone to count on.

Quansah is a decent defender but he is a centre-back, not a right-back.

Trent Alexander-Arnold’s strengths are going forward, while Konsa will get even better thanks to his move to Arsenal.

But Guehi showed some alarming weaknesses on Saturday and his Manchester City team-mate O’Reilly is clearly better in midfield.

As for the keepers, Tuchel wants to look at James Trafford after Jordan Pickford was hit-and-miss at the World Cup.

When England failed to make Euro 2008, Steve McClaren could call on a back four of Micah Richards, Sol Campbell, Rio Ferdinand and Ashley Cole.



Under Graham Taylor, when the Three Lions missed out on the 1994 USA World Cup, there was Lee Dixon, Des Walker, Tony Adams and Stuart Pearce.

Even going back to our failure to qualify for Euro 84 in France, Phil Neal, Terry Butcher, Alvin Martin and Kenny Sansom were the back four and, once again, were more solid than the current lot.

FORMER football star Joey Barton has been tackled by jail bosses over claims a smuggled mobile and tobacco were found in his prison cell.

Barton, 44, could be stripped of his jail privileges after allegedly being caught with the contraband during a search.



But the ex-Man City, Newcastle and QPR midfielder is understood to denying the accusations.

Sources have claimed he could have been forced into hoarding items for gangsters held with him at HMP Liverpool.

Barton, who had managerial stints at Fleetwood Town and Bristol Rovers, is being held on remand after being charged with GBH over an alleged attack near Huyton & Prescot Golf Club on Merseyside in March.



A source said his cell was searched by anti-corruption officers.

They added: “He wasn’t expecting it, guards raced in and turned it over.

“They were acting on intelligence and found a few items including tobacco and a phone and could discipline Barton. But he is denying doing anything wrong.



“And though he doesn’t want to grass up other inmates, bosses are looking at whether he was forced into holding contraband for other people.

“There are some pretty heavy-duty figures in there who could have strong-armed him.

“And he is famous, which always makes you a target inside.”

They went on: “But Barton is likely to be punished whatever the situation was.

“That would mean losing rights to things like watching TV, plus some access to gyms and workshops and time out of his cell.”



The Sun reported in March that Barton was accused of making anti-Muslim comments as he first arrived at the prison in Walton.

The Prison Service confirmed: “Prisoners caught with banned items could be prosecuted, face extra time behind bars and lose privileges.”

Sports.title: KP promises to challenge McCullum as England push to be 'world's best'
Sports.content:
Kevin Pietersen has promised to challenge England white-ball head coach Brendon McCullum in his new role as a specialist mentor to the team, saying it's precisely why he was brought in.

Since retiring as a player in 2018, Pietersen has, at times, been an outspoken critic of the England setup, including when accusing the white-ball team of inadequate preparation on a tour of India last January after McCullum had just taken over.

Pietersen's work with England began with a 3-0 T20 series whitewash of Sri Lanka, before the hosts then also clinched a 2-1 ODI series success over the same side on Sunday. His role with the team will continue through to the 2027 50-over World Cup in just over a year's time.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of England against Sri Lanka in their third ODI at The Oval

"Brendon, when he first called me, I thought I was in trouble because I'd said something, but he said this exact point: 'I'd like you to come in and challenge me,'" Pietersen told Sky Sports Cricket ahead of England's series-clinching 223-run win over Sri Lanka at The Oval.

"He's since said to me: 'I absolutely love the fact that you are inside the rooms and you are picking on things that can make the players better.'

"And at the end of the day, if we can't do that as a coach, try and challenge players to be the best versions of themselves, I think we're letting them down because these guys are too good."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at Kevin Pietersen's incredible insight for England's batters, including the importance of 'rotation of strike'

Pietersen added on his coaching approach: "No stone unturned. There are a few things I don't like. There are many things that I do like, and I think if we can get that balance right, I think that these guys are going to be very, very good.

"That messaging and that constant drive to be the best version of themselves is something that we're drilling down on.

"It's been a brilliant period to understand what actually is happening inside that dressing room. There's a crazy amount of talent up there."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England white-ball coach Brendon McCullum spoke on Kevin Pietersen becoming a mentor for the side and discussed if previous criticism of the team will affect their relationship

McCullum was similarly bullish about his hopes for the 50-over side, specifically with a World Cup in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia in a year's time.

The T20 team have won 22 of their past 25 completed T20 internationals since the start of last summer, assuming the No 1 spot in the world rankings as a result, and McCullum wants similar for the ODI team, currently sixth in the standings.

"I've also found that with a little bit of extra time, I've been able to drill down on some aspects of where you want to take this team and how you want to shape it," McCullum, who was removed as England Test coach earlier this summer, told Sky Sports Cricket.

"At the time, I was very comfortable doing it all [Test and white-ball jobs]. Change happens and my focus now is on how to make this side the best white-ball team in the world.

"We're not there yet. We've got a lot of growth within us and a lot of improvement to make, but there's a determination within the dressing room to be the best team in the world.

"I want us to become the strongest, fastest and most robust cricket teams in the world, one that can play at a high-octane speed.

"The performance we saw today [against Sri Lanka] was brilliant. You go to a World Cup, you got to do it time and time and time again over a long period of time. So that'll be a focus for us over the next little while.

Pietersen: Brook finds game 'too easy' at times

McCullum and Pietersen also both singled out white-ball captain Harry Brook, specifically, for praise.

Brook, despite being vice-captain, was overlooked for the Test captaincy in favour of Joe Root when Ben Stokes retired, but continues to impress in the white-ball role.

"I think he's an outstanding tactician, he's growing as a leader and maturing as a person - and doing it at rapid speed," McCullum said.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Brendon McCullum talks about Harry Brook as a captain for England, singling him out for praise

"Tactically he's outstanding; he's very much the leader of the side. The boys respect him immensely, and not just for his cricket brain but the way he creates the right environment.

"It's like a group of mates playing together, which is which is plain to see when when you watch them play out in the middle."

With the bat against Sri Lanka, Brook notched two half-centuries in the ODI series to go with a 42-ball hundred - England's joint-second-fastest - in the opening T20I.

That innings saw Brook hailed as an "absolute freak" by Ben Stokes, who took to social media to say that, in his opinion, the Yorkshireman's ability outstrips that of Pietersen.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Harry Brook shares his thoughts on Kevin Pietersen's impact on England's white-ball side

But as well as being capable of achieving the incredible, both Brook and Pietersen have had their share of percieved 'brain fade' moments.

Addressing that similarity, Pietersen said: "Looking back at my career, the brain fade moments happen because sometimes you see the game differently. And that's what the fan and the spectator needs to understand... Harry Brook is a player that sees the game differently.

"There are times when Harry Brook stands at the wicket and he goes, 'This is too easy.'

"The one thing that I'm working really hard with Brooky, and will continue to work hard on, is just being better at assessing game situations.

"I will never in my life try and take the flair and that genius out of him."

Sports.title: Kohli passes 15,000 ODI runs as hundred helps India beat West Indies
Sports.content:
Virat Kohli celebrated his return to the international arena by hitting his 55th ODI hundred as India beat West Indies by eight wickets in the series opener on Sunday.

India's star batter - who now only plays this format in international cricket - smashed an unbeaten 139 off 88 balls, including 10 fours and nine sixes, as India successfully chased down 296 in just 41.4 overs.

In doing so, the 37-year-old also became only the second batter after Sachin Tendulkar (18,426) to pass 15,000 runs in ODIs.

"My focus has never been on milestones. Just looking back at the start of my journey, it makes me feel very grateful," Kohli said. "I enjoy each and every minute that I am out there playing for India, and I am able to do the job for my team. As a cricketer, this is all I could dream of."

Skipper Shubman Gill also notched a century, scoring 110 off 108 deliveries as India registered an easy win - clinched with a Kohli six - to go 1-0 up in the three-match series.

Earlier, West Indies had posted 295-7 from their 50 overs after being put into bat. Opener Justin Greaves (101 off 108) scored his maiden ODI ton, sharing in an impressive 135-run opening partnership with John Campbell (62 off 60) inside the first 20 overs.

Wrist spinner Kuldeep Yadav (4-40) ultimately accounted for both as he wreaked havoc in the middle overs to see West Indies reduced to 198-5 by the 36th.

Amir Jangoo's unbeaten 58 off 43 balls helped revive the innings, but their target of 296 ultimately proved an under-par one on a batter-friendly pitch.

It was a quick-fire chase for India as openers Gill and Rohit Sharma added 74 off 72 balls, Sharma scoring 32 off 35 before he fell to Alzarri Joseph (1-81) in the 12th over.

Kohli came to the crease and promptly eased his way to fifty in only 40 balls, hitting the 15,000-milestone on the way - the fastest to do it at 303 innings, compared to Tendulkar's 377.

He and Gill put on 151 off 132 balls for the second wicket before the captain departed against the run of play to Roston Chase (1-64) in the 34th over.

But Kohli cruised to a 74-ball hundred, before finishing the game in style with 8.2 overs to spare. Kohli's nine sixes were his most in an ODI innings.

Guwahati and Chandigarh will host the second and third ODIs on Wednesday and Saturday, followed by a five-match T20 series starting on October 6.

Sports.title: Thompson strike seals Chelsea win to end Arsenal's unbeaten run
Sports.content:
Alyssa Thompson scored the only goal as Chelsea secured a 1-0 win against Arsenal to end their unbeaten streak in the Women's Super League.

Arsenal failed to make their early dominance count after striking the post twice through Kim Little and Mariona Caldentey before Thompson broke the deadlock at Stamford Bridge.

Keira Walsh's strike from distance was initially well kept out by Anneke Borbe, but the goalkeeper was left helpless when Thompson pounced in the box to fire home the rebound in emphatic style.

The Gunners - who had drawn their last two WSL matches - improved in the second half, with Chloe Kelly's angled drive blocked and Alessia Russo's shot charged down, but the hosts saw out the closing stages for a third WSL win.

Their unbeaten streak in the WSL, stretching back to October 2025, came to an end with it. The Gunners had not tasted defeat in their last 20 games before their trip to west London.

Victory takes Chelsea to within two points of league leaders Manchester City at the top of the table, while Arsenal are already seven points adrift ahead of their meeting with the champions on October 4.

Image: Alyssa Thompson of Chelsea celebrates her opener with team-mates

Slegers 'disappointed' but believes in her players despite struggles

Arsenal boss Renee Slegers speaking to Sky Sports:

"Very disappointed. We know it's a tough game, Chelsea away. I think we did well in the first half in the physical battle and dominated until their goal. We found it hard in the second half and it cost us more energy.

"[We will] work hard, reflect and go forward. I want to take everything away from the players because I think they're at their very best when they're light. There is so much quality in the squad."

On what isn't clicking for Arsenal currently: "It's a cocktail of things. It's everything. Technical and psychological. We're looking at it. I believe in these players. The goals and the points will come. I believe in them."

On the title race: "We have to earn the right to talk about this because we've lost too many points at the moment. Look at the next game and get the points."

Are Arsenal's title chances over already?

Sky Sports' Dan Long:

It seems a touch early to definitely say whether or not Arsenal's title chances are over already, but their start has left a lot to be desired.

Four games in, they have scored only twice and one of those goals - in the 1-1 draw with Man Utd last weekend - wasn't scored until the fifth minute of second-half stoppage time.

And now their unbeaten run in the WSL, which started all the way back on October 12 last year, has been ended by Chelsea.

It leaves the Gunners seven points adrift of leaders Man City already.

Head coach Renee Slegers was asked about that topic after full-time at Stamford Bridge and she said she wanted to "take the pressure off" her players.

"I believe in these players. The goals will come and the points will come as well," she said.

"We have to earn the right again to talk about this [the title race] because we've lost too many points."

With a trip to City up next on October 4, the week ahead feels like a crucial one in the north Londoners' season.

Sports.title: Australia suffer ODI series defeat to South Africa
Sports.content:
Australia fell to an ODI series defeat to South Africa with a game to spare as they were beaten by 32 runs in the second ODI match of three in Johannesburg on Sunday.

David Miller (142 off 93 balls) and Temba Bavuma (103 off 116) each smashed centuries for South Africa as they set the visitors a massive 366-run target after being inserted at the toss.

Australia looked well placed early on in their reply, with openers Mitch Marsh (84 off 53) and ​Travis Head (85 off 76) setting the tone by blazing the bowling to all parts.

But ultimately the tourists' middle-order batting issues and struggles against spin were again laid bare. From 191-2 in the 25th over, they added only 62 for the loss of four wickets in the next 15 and a bit overs to stumble to 253-6.

That left Australia needing another 113 runs to win from the final 10 overs and, despite a late counter-punch from Xavier Bartlett (50 off 28), they'd eventually be bowled out for 333 in the final over.

Keshav Maharaj took 2-54, Bjorn Fortuin 2-70 and Aiden Markram 1-55 among the Proteas' spin options. Seamer Lizaad Williams 3-54 and Marco Jansen 2-53.

"It's certainly an area where we need to improve and we're well aware of that," Australia captain ‌Marsh said. "I thought we set up our innings really well in both games but we haven't been able to execute during those middle ‌phases.

"It's a great learning curve, especially for some of our younger players. But you also have to give South Africa full credit for the way they've bowled during those periods."

Miller's eighth ODI ton - containing 12 fours and nine sixes - and captain Bavuma's sixth had helped South Africa to a score of 365-9 from their 50 overs.

Jack Edwards, playing in only his second ODI, grabbed 5-67 and Josh Hazlewood, who dismissed Aiden Markram off the first ball for a golden duck, took 3-70.

Australia, who haven't won a bilateral ODI series against South Africa since 2014, will look for a consolation win in the last game in Potchefstroom on Wednesday. They've lost 19 of their last 25 ODIs against their hosts.

"It was another really good ⁠all-round team performance," Bavuma said. "It started with the bat. ​Conditions were a little tricky up front but we managed to get through ​that period and build towards a good total.

"David played an unbelievable innings and then the bowlers did their job as well."

Sports.title: Imperious Banton century propels England to Sri Lanka series victory
Sports.content:
Tom Banton posted an imperious 126 off just 105 balls to guide England to a dominant 223-run win in the third ODI against Sri Lanka to secure a 2-1 series victory at the Oval.

Banton top scored with his career-best but was aided by sizeable contributions by skipper Harry Brook (77 off 66) and the in-form Jordan Cox (76 off 52) as the batting side set the tourists a mammoth target of 356 after their 50 overs, with Dilhara Fernando (3-52) the pick of the bowlers - albeit with two of his wickets coming with the final two balls of the innings.

That target loomed even larger over Sri Lanka's innings when Sonny Baker nicked off Pathum Nissanka (1) for his maiden ODI wicket with just the eighth ball of their innings.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch every boundary from Tom Banton's maiden ODI century

From there the wickets started to tumble for Sri Lanka who - despite the best efforts of captain Kusal Mendis (35 off 26) - went from 36-1 to 82-6 in just 10 overs, including the confusing run-out dismissal of Pavan Rathnayake (18), which was still given as out despite Jordan Cox taking the bails off before Archer's direct-hit throw dismantled the stumps.

The impressive bowling of Liam Dawson (3-17) and Gus Atkinson (2-26) then ensured Sri Lanka's tail went out with a 50-run whimper, handing England the series victory and marking a successful end of the home summer for Brendon McCullum's side after 12 wins in 14 white-ball games.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Pavan Rathnayake was run out by Jofra Archer after confusion reigned as Jordan Cox broke the stumps early

Banton brilliance headlines complete England performance

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ben Duckett went early for England as Sri Lanka's Dilshan Madushanka smashed the stumps

Despite England's eventual victory, it took just eight balls for Sri Lanka to take their first wicket as Ben Duckett (0) was clean bowled by Dilshan Madushanka (1-49), before Joe Root was dismissed by Janith Liyanage in an uncharacteristically stiff cameo that saw him notch just 18 off 37 balls.

It was then the partnership of Brook and player-of-the-match Banton that made the difference for England, putting on 150 runs in a lucrative partnership that was eventually ended when the former was caught on the boundary by Dunith Wellalage.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Joe Root fell leg before as Sri Lanka claimed their second wicket against England in their third ODI

Banton's majestic innings - featuring 21 boundaries and including five sixes - came to a conclusion when his effort to hit a sixth maximum was caught by Malinga at long-on.

But England were not done there - alongside Will Jacks (25 off 21), Cox spearheaded a late flurry of runs, notching his half-century off 42 balls before Fernando took his and Dawson's wickets with the final two balls of the 49th over, leaving England in the ascendancy after posting a formidable score of 355-7.

Sri Lanka were immediately left reeling after Baker's early wicket and found it difficult to recover, with no batter scoring above 20 bar their captain Mendis, with their woes being immediately compounded by the controversial run out of Pavan Rathnayake.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sonny Baker got an early wicket within his first two balls for England against Sri Lanka in their 3rd ODI clash

Cox appeared to have made a mishap after taking the bails off the stumps before he was in control of the ball, but - after a near five-minute period of discussion involving both umpires and players - Archer's direct-hit throw uprooting the stump was ruled legitimate.

His dismissal was followed by that of Charith Asalanka and Wellalage within the next eight balls, leaving Sri Lanka on the brink of defeat at 82-6 with no recognised batters left, before the excellent work of Dawson - taking three of the last four Sri Lanka wickets - ensured England's dominant victory was confirmed with 21.5 overs to spare.

Brook: That was a near-perfect performance

Image: Baker took his maiden ODI wicket

England captain Harry Brook, speaking to Sky Sports:

"I thought that was a near-perfect performance there - I thought everyone chipped in and it was an exceptional win.

"There was some tough periods, but I thought the patience we showed, it was exceptional.

"We want to be able to adapt to conditions every game. Every surface has been slightly different. That is the side we want to be - we want to win when they are not in our favour and when they are, we want to nail sides.

"We are building towards a squad where someone can come into roles and fill it exceptionally well. We are building to a strong squad and I have full trust in anyone who comes in."

Mendis: We made too many mistakes

Image: Mendis top scored for Sri Lanka for the second successive game

Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis:

"We struggled with the batting and then we made some mistakes in the field, including me.

"I think we played good cricket in the second ODI and when go to Pakistan after this, we need to be better.

"We made too many mistakes."

Sports.title: Bellamy 'hurting' after Denmark beat Wales comfortably
Sports.content:
Craig Bellamy says he is “really hurting” after Wales were beaten 2-0 in Copenhagen by a dominant Denmark to leave them bottom of their Nations League group

Both of Denmark's goals came from set pieces delivered by Brentford midfielder Mikkel Damsgaard with Ben Davies turning into his own net shortly after the break before Gustav Iskasen's deflected strike put the game beyond doubt.

Wales were second best throughout and could have been behind in the first half with Damsgaard striking the post from range moments after Isaksen had a volley ruled out by VAR for a marginal offside from Rasmus Hojlund in the build-up.

Craig Bellamy's depleted side battled to a 1-0 defeat against Portugal in Lisbon on Thursday but they were utterly outclassed by Denmark in Copenhagen in a result that paints a bleak picture for their hopes in Nations League Group A4.

Wales have failed to register a single goal or point in their first two games and they face an uphill battle if they are to avoid relegation from this group.

Denmark were under similar pressure after being beaten by Norway on Thursday, and there was turmoil in the camp after captain Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg openly questioned the team's tactics, but they rose to the occasion and could easily have won more comfortably.

The only negative for Denmark was an injury to Manchester United's Patrick Dorgu, who was forced off after 30 minutes and headed straight down the tunnel.

Wales have no let up as they face Norway and Erling Haaland on Thursday in their third Nations League match. Norway were beaten 2-1 by Portugal in Oslo later on Sunday.

Key moments from Copenhagen

24: DENMARK GOAL RULED OUT BY VAR! Isaksen's volley is chalked off for a marginal offside on Hojlund.

27: OFF THE POST! Damsgaard rattles a shot off the frame of the goal for Denmark.

30: INJURY! Dorgu forced off with an apparent injury problem.

43: VITAL SAVE! Filip Jorgensen produces a big hand to keep out Connor Roberts' close-range effort.

53: GOAL! Denmark lead through a Davies own-goal after Damsgaard's free-kick.

66: GOAL! Denmark double their lead through Isaksen's deflected strike at another set piece.

Bellamy: It will be a tough watch back

Wales boss Craig Bellamy:

"I'm really hurting. When you see an athletic team run over you a little bit… but then, will we improve? I think we will.

"This team will get better, these players will keep improving. There are young ones coming in well after I'm gone.

"For me now it's just focus, two more games to go. How can I help you improve for the next two games, but also how can I improve?

"I'm probably more loving when I'm losing, I'm probably more of a pain in the backside when I'm winning.

"I said to the players before the game, 'this is going to be tougher than Portugal'. It was a different challenge, but a very difficult one. The best team won overall.

"As disappointed as I am with that, the result I probably think was fair. We move on. It will be a tough watch back.

"How the players put their bodies on the line was brilliant. They are really special for that. I really admire that, but I want more."

Ampadu: Disappointing night for Wales

Wales midfielder Ethan Ampadu to BBC Sport:

"Disappointing night for us. Always going to be difficult against a top team away from home. But we didn't really put in our levels. We gave everything we could.

"We could have been tidier on the ball, especially in transitions. We didn't create enough to score today.

"Frustrating to concede [both goals from set pieces]. We pride ourselves on being difficult to beat on set pieces and work so hard on it. We just didn't defend well enough today at set pieces."

Sports.title: Hearn: Fury vs AJ press conference not 'confirmed'
Sports.content:
