Sports.title: The new Miracle at Medinah: Team USA completes wild comeback to win the Presidents Cup in front of Trump
Sports.content:
Team USA completed one of the greatest comebacks in Presidents Cup history to overcome their international rivals in front of a raucous crowd at Medinah.

The Americans headed into Sunday singles three points down and at risk of a humbling loss, but Scottie Scheffler and Co won eight of the 12 singles matches to seal an 11th straight win.

The day began with a rousing speech from Donald Trump, before the players went out and stormed back, with Jacob Bridgeman clinching the trophy for his country.

There were key rallies on the back nine by two-time major champion Collin Morikawa and 21-year-old rookie Jackson Koivun.

Outplayed over three days in team matches, the Americans leaned on their strength in singles to make up a three-point deficit.

President Trump was on the first tee for the start of all 12 singles matches, and he kept his speech short. 'It's going to be a very interesting game of golf,' he said.

Team USA celebrates after Jackson Koivun secured a huge win for his country at Medinah

Jacob Bridgeman holed the winning putt as America surged back from three points down

The day began with a speech from Donald Trump, who watched the start of all 12 matches

The president had hot-footed it to Illinois fresh from watching Texas beat Tennessee in Knoxville on Saturday, and he drew roaring applause from the packed grandstands at Medinah.

Dressed in a dark suit and red tie, Trump smiled, pumped his fists, and blew kisses to the excited crowd as spectators broke out into deafening chants of 'USA! USA!'

Taking to the microphone ahead of the Sunday singles matches, Trump poked fun at reports that he had requested a 15-minute speech window from the PGA Tour.

'You know, the fake news media will say I got a very bad reception. We got a good reception!' Trump told the cheering gallery.

'He [PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp] said, could you make a short speech? I said, no, I don't have the courage to make a speech - these people want to see golf, they don't want to hear speeches!

''I'll only say this: Our country is doing great, better than ever before.'

His Sunday arrival brought enhanced security measures across Medinah, with gates opening at 8 a.m. as the Secret Service implemented tight restrictions.

Koivun celebrates after birdieing the 12th hole on his way to a big win in the Sunday singles

Trump continued his whirlwind weekend of sport on Sunday after attending the Texas game

The lighthearted quip came after Golfweek reported on Saturday that Trump had asked organizers for 15 minutes to address the crowd before the start of play.

Trump stepped aside quickly to let the action begin, as Brandt Snedeker's U.S. squad looked to battle back from a 10.5 - 7.5 deficit against Geoff Ogilvy's International team.

On Sunday, it was Cameron Young and Justin Thomas who set the tone early. Scottie Scheffler took down Nico Echavarria with a show of pure sportsmanship when a spectator disrupted the Colombian's swing.

Patrick Cantlay had another moment, as he always seem to do in this competition, holing a birdie putt from just inside 60 feet on the par-3 16th against hard-luck Adam Scott.

Scottie Scheffler was another of the Americans who secured a big win at Medinah on Sunday

Trump is accompanied by Secret Service as he walks to make his speech at the Presidents Cup

Outside the gates at Medinah, some anti-Trump protestors spoke out against the president

Five matches remained on the course - the Americans were 1 up in three of them, the other two were all square. All the Internationals had to do was find three points from them. The Americans simply refused to budge.

Koivun was 2 down through 10 holes to the Internationals' top performer this week, Si Woo Kim, when he won three straight holes to flip the color to American red on the board. The kid drilled his tee shot on the 18th, and twirled his iron when he knew the approach was pure. He wound up with a 2-up victory, and then it was a matter of time.

The clinching point came from Jacob Bridgeman, who rolled in a 3-foot par putt on the 18th green for a 1-up victory over Min Woo Lee, assuring the Americans the 15 1/2 points they needed.

Sports.title: Ireland stars REFUSE to shake hands of Israeli opponents and bow their heads during national anthem ahead of controversial clash after goalkeeper withdrew from squad in protest at 'atrocities in Gaza'
Sports.content:
Ireland's players bowed their heads during the Israel national anthem and did not shake hands with their opponents before the controversial Nations League clash in Hungary. The fixture has been shrouded in controversy after the Irish team and officials came under huge pressure to stage a boycott due to Israel’s military actions in Gaza. Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu withdrew from the squad, with the Bolton star saying ‘I am a man of strong faith and try my best to be a person of character and principle’. 'My decision is based purely upon my belief that the killing of innocent people is wrong,' he addded. 'It is important to note that my stance is not in opposition to the Israeli people or the Jewish community but against the atrocities in the region.' Players voted to fulfil the fixture and also agreed to wear black armbands in recognition of all the lives lost in the conflict. Ireland also decided against giving a pennant to Israel to mark the match - a standard gesture in all international fixtures. The customary pre-match handshake did not take place and during the playing of the Israel anthem, Ireland's starting XI looked towards the floor in unison - as did their substitutes. The Ireland XI look to the floor during the playing of the Israel national anthem Israel's players stood for the anthem as Ireland's bowed their heads The Irish side did stand proud for their own national anthem Ireland's substitutes and staff also looked at the floor during Israel's anthem, with the squad having voted to play the match Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu withdrew from the squad due to Israel's actions in Gaza Heimir Hallgrimsson was heavily criticised in Israel for saying Ireland are 'playing against genocide' Ireland won 3-0 after first-half goals from Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan, who took off his black armband and kissed it when celebrating. There were no handshakes as full time and Ireland’s players were booed as they left the field. Manager Heimir Hallgrimsson had also said that ‘nobody is comfortable playing these games for many reasons’ and, earlier in the week, said his team were ‘playing against genocide’. A training session on Saturday was delayed by five hours after players decided whether to boycott the match which was held in Debrecen, Hungary, with Israel playing in neutral venues due to the conflict. FAI chief executive David Courell said a ‘significant majority’ voted to play. UEFA rules mean teams must name at least three goalkeepers in their squad and Bazunu's withdrawal meant that Jimmy Dunne, the QPR centre back, was named as a keeper on the official team-sheet. Irish broadcaster RTE cut back its screening of the game with no studio punditry, no advertising and only using commentary from an international feed. Many pubs in Ireland refused to show the game and there were protests outside the team hotel in Dublin earlier in the week. Ireland are set to play Israel again on Sunday but it will be behind closed doors at a neutral venue in Serbia.

Sports.title: Main victims of Man City's 'cheating' revealed: Who suffered the MOST from the club's glory years - and how much it cost them - after Premier League's seismic guilty verdict
Sports.content:
In their seminal book Soccernomics, published in 2009, Simon Kuper and Stefan Szymanski conclude that the single biggest predictor for a team's success is how much they spend on wages. Pay more and you'll likely win more.

Around the same time, UEFA put out its own report into the link between finances and future triumphs across Europe's major leagues. 'There is a strong correlation between club spending and success on the pitch and is one of the biggest factors determining the likelihood of success,' it found. 'Money does not guarantee success but it does improve the probability of victory.'

Apropos of absolutely nothing, it was also in 2009-10, the second season under their new Abu Dhabi owners, that Manchester City's wage bill jumped by £50million to nearly twice the Premier League average. Before their arrival, City paid £54m in wages and the top-flight average was £60m. Now, it was £133m when the average was still only £70m. By the time 2012-13 ticked around, with a league title under their belts, they were paying 2.6 times the Premier League average. The season before that, the iconic final-day drama against QPR, they paid 2.4 times it.

As the bombshell news broke on Friday that City had been found guilty of the vast majority of the 115 Premier League charges, something else became clear: over that nine-season period from 2009, they had bought their way to the top and done so unfairly. The question now is at what cost - not just to themselves, of course, but to other clubs in the process.

Arsenal, Tottenham, Liverpool and Manchester United all served legal notices last year reserving their right to take action should City be found guilty. They will argue, should the verdict stand, that City's misdemeanours cost them titles, trophies, European qualification and, above all when it comes to these things, money.

So, just how much has City's rule breaking cost their rivals?

First, some parameters. You can argue, quite convincingly, that City's actions over those nine seasons built the very foundations for the rampant success that followed under Pep Guardiola and that, without them, despite his genius, they would unlikely have had the platform or finances in place to achieve it, but, for now, we will stick to that period between 2009-10 and 2017-18.

So, apologies in advance to Mikel Arteta for those two second-placed finishes behind City and sorry, too, to Jurgen Klopp for those two runners-up spots with 97 and 92 points, and to Watford for their FA Cup final defeat.

Every Premier League side during this time can feel aggrieved about something, whether it's the few million quid difference for finishing a place lower than they might. Clubs could also argue that missing out on cash or European football would have cost them in the transfer market too and they could have signed bigger, better superstars for long-term success. That, again, is far too deep a rabbit hole.

What it does all show, however, is that things are about to get messy.

Who are the biggest victims from Manchester City's success down the years?

TOTTENHAM HOTSPUR

Trust Spurs to be perhaps the biggest loser from all of this. Spurs missed out on the Champions League four times during the years where City are said to have been up to no good.

Tottenham finished fifth in 2010-11, 2012-13 and 2014-15. The worst of all of them was 2011-12 when they finished inside the top four but, in true Spurs fashion, didn't qualify for the Champions League because Chelsea won the competition despite finishing sixth.

Take City out of this - or, at least, turn them back into the midtable scrappers they were before Abu Dhabi's instant cash - and that's four seasons in Europe's elite competition should they have made it through the play-off round.

City went out in the group stages in two of those Champions League seasons and still took home about £24m in each of them. When they reached the semi-finals in 2015-16, they banked £61.2m.

Even if Spurs had failed to get out of the group in any of them that's still £100m. Spurs received £2.7m for their Europa League campaign in 2011-12, Manchester United earned 10 times as much for crashing out in the Champions League group stages that season.

Tottenham have missed out on the Champions League four times because of Man City - including under Harry Redknapp

MANCHESTER UNITED

In another life, Manchester United might have 22 league titles instead of 20. Sir Alex Ferguson's side lost out to City on goal difference in that remarkable 2011-12 season but, in this parallel universe, poor Martin Tyler never got his 'Aguerrrooo' moment.

United were runners up to City's 100-point monsters in 2017-18, albeit still some 19 points behind.

In merit payments alone, that tots up to a little shy of £3m, and we're not even beginning to think of any extra money on merchandise or open-top bus parades.

United also missed out on qualifying for the Champions League in 2015-16 as, once again, City pipped them on goal difference to budge the Red Devils into fifth and the Europa League.

Jose Mourinho would lead United to the trophy the following season of course, pocketing them about £38m in the process, but even that is less than the £48m City earned from reaching the last 16 of the Champions League.

Manchester United would have won a Premier League title under Jose Mourinho

LIVERPOOL

Say goodbye to the Steven Gerrard slip as well. Liverpool finished two points behind City in that fateful 2013-14 season under Brendan Rodgers. The difference between first and second that season, in purely financial terms, was about £1.2m in merit payments but, again, the Reds will surely attempt to claim that ending what would have been a 24-year wait for a title, instead of the 30 years it took them in the end, would have seen them cash in far and wide.

Liverpool lost in the final of the League Cup to City in 2016 on penalties too. Now, of course, what's to say that Everton, who City beat in the semi-finals, wouldn't have got the better of them. Winning the competition would only have gained them an extra £50,000 in prize money but, crucially, would have booked their place in the Europa League. They didn't have European football the following season, finishing eighth and also losing to Sevilla in the final of the competition that year for which they earned about £32m.

The Reds also finished sixth in 2010-11, leaving them with no European football the following season. Take City away, and they're back in the Europa League too.

Steven Gerrard's slip against Chelsea would not have mattered - Liverpool would have won the Premier League title anyway

ARSENAL

At the end of the 2016-17 season, Arsenal's run of 20 successive Champions League qualifications under Arsene Wenger came to an end. They finished fifth, a point behind Liverpool, and three behind third-placed City.

In this life, the run goes on. The gain an extra £2m for a higher league finish and Champions League spoils via the play-offs. The Gunners earned £33.5m for reaching the Europa League semis the following season while City took home £54.6m for reaching the quarter-finals of the Champions League.

Arsenal can also add the 2018 League Cup to their cabinet, too. Again, only £50,000 more in prize money and they had already qualified for the Europe but, still, nice to have some more silverware.

Arsenal's run of qualifying for the Champions League under Arsene Wenger would have continued

EVERTON

Not only might the Toffees have a shot at Liverpool in the League Cup final in 2016, but they also fell just short of European qualification multiple times. Everton finished fifth under Roberto Martinez in 2013-14, settling for Europa League instead of Champions League. That earned them about £5m, far less than the grandest stage not to mention £1.2m for one lower place.

The season before, they finished sixth and got no European football at all - without City, they do. In 2009-10, when Portsmouth, the FA Cup runners-up, were refused a UEFA licence, their Europa League place went instead to the team that finished seventh. That was Liverpool. Without City, it would have been Everton.

In 2011-12, they finished seventh. England's quota was full after Chelsea won the Champions League from sixth. Without City, Everton get Europe again.

Everton would have been playing in the Champions League and Europe several times

CHELSEA

Similarly, Chelsea had to make do with fifth place instead of fourth in 2017-18. As a consolation, they went on to win the Europa League the following season under Maurizio Sarri, which brought them in £41m.

Oh and don't forget the Community Shield in 2012. A trophy's a trophy.

Tony Pulis' Stoke City lost to Man City in the 2011 FA Cup final - they may have won that!

SUNDERLAND AND STOKE

I spent some time in Sunderland earlier this summer, as the club prepared for its first European adventure in more than half a century. How different things might have been. The Black Cats lost to City in the League Cup final in 2014 with the winners earning a place in the Europa League that would likely have banked them £5m. Four years later, they were in League One.

Stoke lost to City in the 2011 FA Cup final. They still got into the Europa League as City were in the Champions League but the result still cost them nearly £1m in prize money.

A belated congratulations to Tony Pulis on his first and only major trophy.

Sports.title: San Francisco 49ers injury curse gets even worse as Mike Evans is carted off while struggling to BREATHE
Sports.content:
San Francisco 49ers star Mike Evans was carted to the locker room after suffering a brutal injury that appeared to leave him struggling to breathe on the sideline.

WR1 Evans is just the latest Niner star to be struck down, as their brutal injury luck threatens to derail their season.

Evans' latest blow came in the second quarter against the Arizona Cardinals when he was clattered by safety Budda Baker after making a catch.

He initially played on but was then seen being helped to the sideline by trainers, clutching his ribs as he limped off the field.

Injury analyst Jeff Mueller posted a clip of Evans on X, alongside the caption: 'Mike Evans appears injured and is in a ton of pain. Almost looks like he can't breathe. Just dropped down to a knee on the sideline and trying to catch his breath. Hopefully not a lung or vital organ issue.'

There is no further update on the nature of Evans' injury, but soon after he was spotted sitting on the back of a cart which transported him to the locker room.

Mike Evans is carted back to the locker room after suffering an injury in the second quarter

Evans appeared to suffer the injury while being tackled by Cardinals safety Budda Baker

Mike Evans appears injured and is in a ton of pain. Almost looks like he can’t breathe. Just dropped down to a knee on the sideline and trying to catch his breath.



Hopefully not a lung or vital organ issue. pic.twitter.com/IYNprrCghD — Jeff Mueller, PT, DPT (@jmthrivept) September 27, 2026

In the lead-up to the game against the Cardinals, Evans was day-to-day with a hip injury, but it is unclear whether his latest issue is related to that.

Last month he was dealing with a left quad strain and a groin strain, while he missed more than half of last season after needing surgery on a broken collarbone suffered in Week 7 against Detroit, while playing for Tampa Bay.

Evans' injury on Sunday came shortly after he had scored a touchdown - his second of the season - for a 49ers offense in desperate need for its stars to remain on the field.

As it stands, Demarcus Robinson is not practicing with a high ankle sprain. Rookie wideout De'Zhaun Stribling got injured in Week 1, Christian Kirk is still 'a couple of weeks away' from being healthy, and Ricky Pearsall is in the second month of a nine-month recovery period after undergoing knee surgery in mid-August.

On the other side of the ball, star defensive end Nick Bosa was ruled out for 'multiple weeks' with a calf injury suffered in practice earlier this week.

Bosa is one of six members of the Niners defense to go down in just the past fortnight. In just the last two weeks, they have lost Alfred Collins to a season-ending torn patellar tendon, Sam Okuayinonu to a broken foot, James Thompson Jr to a high ankle sprain, Romello Height to a broken hand and CJ West to a bone chip in his knee.

Additionally, Mykel Williams is still on the PUP list from a torn ACL he suffered last season, leaving the defense incredibly stretched.

Conspiracy theories about the 49ers' injury curse have swirled for years, bursting into the public consciousness early this year when the team even launched an investigation into the electrical substation alongside the practice facility.

Evans knelt to the ground and appeared to be struggling to breathe as he hobbled off the field

A viral X thread from January even sparked an investigation into the substation by the team

General manager John Lynch told the media the organization would investigate 'everything' into why so many stars were being struck down by injury, later insisting that it was a 'big nothing burger.'

The investigation revealed that 'EMF exposure was approximately 400 times below what would constitute an unsafe working environment', yet the injuries have continued to pile up.

Even players themselves have questioned whether the substation may be behind their continued bad luck, with Dre Greenlaw admitting that he thought 'Man what the hell going on over here?' before ultimately deciding to re-sign with the team.

Previously, Kendrick Bourne was asked about the mounting injuries after George Kittle suffered a torn Achilles, and he joked to reporters: 'Yeah, it's that power plant.'

Sports.title: 'He did so much for everyone': Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky pays emotional tribute to agent and mentor Ludek Miklosko after West Ham star's death at 64
Sports.content:
Tottenham goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky paid a personal tribute to Ludek Miklosko ahead of England’s game against Czechia.

West Ham hero Miklosko, who died this month at the age of 64, had a great influence on Kinsky’s early career as an agent and mentor.

'Probably from the age of 10-18, then he left the agency to become sporting director at Banik Ostrava and I left as well,' said the 23-year-old Spurs keeper.

'He was one of those people who I really respected and admired. For what he achieved in football and especially in life. He was an honest, kind and respectful person.'

Miklosko’s death after a battle with cancer was confirmed as Spurs prepared for a Carabao Cup tie at Liverpool.

'He is very inspiring,' said Kinsky. 'He had huge experience and was someone I trusted. He was someone apart from my family who I discussed all the big, important decisions in my football career, especially when I was young, aged 14-15 and I had some offers to join big European clubs.

Antonin Kinsky has paid tribute to former West Ham and Czechia goalkeeper Ludek Miklosko

The current Tottenham and Czechia stopper described Miklosko as 'very inspiring' and helpful

'Eventually I didn’t because I believed I had a bigger chance to get to the highest level if I get to professional football firstly in the Czech Republic and after I become the best here to go abroad.

'It was a big decision, and he was part of it, and he was there for more things like this.

'He also organised a lot of summer goalkeeper camps in the Czech Republic with goalkeeper coaches from Premier League teams and other clubs. This was a great thing for us young kids who were dreaming about getting to European football, to see what the training there look like. He did so much for everyone.'

Kinsky’s father Antonin is a former keeper who played in the Czech and Russian leagues and won international caps and whose career overlapped with Miklosko’s.

The pioneering Miklosko was 28 years old when he left Banik Ostrava for West Ham in 1990 and remained in London until his career ended with three years at Queens Park Rangers.

He had retired by the time Kinsky junior was born in 2003 but remained an icon in Czech football and an inspiration for goalkeepers who followed his footsteps, including Pavel Srnicek and Petr Cech.

'All those are great keepers,' said Kinsky. 'It’s why they were able to get to Premier league and make an impact. Petr Cech also gave me huge motivation and inspiration.'

The three Czechia goalkeepers in the squad to face Thomas Tuchel’s team on Tuesday have strong connections to English football.

Lukas Hornicek is at Newcastle and Matej Hovar of PSV Eindhoven spent five years at Manchester United from the age of 18 and had spells on loan at Swindon and Burton Albion.

Sports.title: Now THAT'S a hydration break! Legends match is stopped so players can drink BEER and a shot in hilarious scenes
Sports.content:
Now THAT'S a hydration break! Legends match is stopped so players can drink BEER and a shot in hilarious scenes

A legends match was halted by a hydration break with a difference, as Real Madrid and Werder Bremen players were presented with a beer and a shot on the pitch.

Hydration breaks during the World Cup had largely been booed by fans in stadiums due to matches being delayed as players took on water and received tactical advice from their coaches.

The hydration break at Werder Bremen's Weserstadion on Saturday, however, was warmly received.

Play was halted in the 32nd minute of the match, which was aimed at marking the 100th anniversary of Werder Bremen's stadium.

Servers, who wore white shirts and black aprons, emerged and walked down the touchline carrying trays.

A beer and a shot were visible on the trays, which were then presented to the players on the field.

Der Traum einiger Fußballer! 🤩😅



Werder Legenden gegen Real Madrid Leyendas live auf Sky Sport Bundesliga, Sky Sport Top Event sowie auf dem Sky YouTube-Kanal! 🍿✅ pic.twitter.com/1G6wBpx9Ya — Sky Sport (@SkySportDE) September 26, 2026

Werder Bremen and Real Madrid legends were presented with a beer and Malteser shot during a hydration break on Saturday

Former Werder Bremen star Ailton was seen enjoying a beer on the pitch during the break

Brazilian striker Ailton, who helped Werder Bremen win the Bundesliga title back in 2004, was seen picking up and drinking the beer during the break in play.

The halting of the match in the 32nd minute was a tribute to former referee Wolf-Dieter Ahlenfelder.

Ahlenfelder famously blew the whistle for half-time in the 32nd minute of a match at the stadium between Werder and Hannover back in 1975.

The referee, who was persuaded to continue the match, later revealed he had a beer and a Malteser shot at lunch before the game. Ahlenfelder, however, denied being drunk during the match.

A beer and Malteser shot reportedly became a popular drink around the stadium following the incident.

The legends match featured former Werder Bremen stars Diego, Naldo, Ailton and Per Mertesacker.

Claude Makelele, Pepe, Christian Karembeu and Esteban Cambiasso were among those to feature for Real Madrid.

Werder Bremen ultimately emerged as 4-3 winners in the match.

Sports.title: Man Utd chief Sir Jim Ratcliffe to settle £180m dispute after 'months of heated arguments'
Sports.content:
Man Utd chief Sir Jim Ratcliffe to settle £180m dispute after 'months of heated arguments'

Manchester United co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe reportedly wants to resolve a £180million legal dispute involving Ineos after what are said to have been 18 months of heated arguments

View 2 Images Sir Jim Ratcliffe is said to be in talks over settling with Sir Ben Ainslie (Image: PA)

Sir Ben Ainslie and Sir Jim Ratcliffe reportedly want to settle their legal row out of court rather than wait over 12 months for the next available trial date. Ineos sued the four-time Olympic champion sailor's Athena Racing team in March over their use of a racing yacht they claim to have spent £180million on.

‌



Ainslie and Ratcliffe stopped working together last January. They teamed up for two America's Cups in Auckland in 2021 and in Barcelona in 2024.

‌



Manchester United's minority shareholder previously committed to a third. However, that all changed last year after the pair fell out.

‌



Eric Cantona teams up with Gary Lineker as Man Utd chief Sir Jim Ratcliffe slammed again READ MORE :

Man Utd announce record revenues but debt rises as Old Trafford grass goes on sale for £125! READ MORE :

More than a year after proceedings commenced, Ainslie told The Telegraph in Naples this weekend: "A lot of water has flowed under the bridge over the last 18 months.

"We had a mutual desire to win the America's Cup, and I'm confident we'll be able to find a way to resolve this before it goes to court."

As initially reported by The Telegraph, the earliest available slots for hearings and trials at the Commercial Court that are anticipated to run longer than a week are from 15 November 2027. That would be four months after next year's America's Cup concludes.

‌



Ainslie's defence against the High Court proceedings initiated by Ratcliffe alleges that he demanded "all of [the team's] assets and intellectual property" be transferred to him in exchange for his continued backing. The filing claims Ineos Sport chairman Rob Nevin "stated to Sir Ben: 'This is what Jim wants.

View 2 Images Sir Ben Ainslie and Sir Jim Ratcliffe teamed up in 2018 (Image: Lloyd Images, Getty Images)

"We have a phrase at Ineos: 'scorched earth'. It means that if you don't give Jim what he wants, he will burn your house down' (or words to that effect)."

‌



Chief executive Jean-Claude Blanc is also alleged to have confronted Ainslie alongside chairman Nevin. Their legal representatives did not dispute that.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Ineos stated in submitted court documents: "It is admitted that Mr Nevin indicated that Sir Jim would not back down (and had only ever done so in a dispute concerning the People's Republic of China) and in that context referred to 'scorched earth'.

Article continues below

"But it is denied that these comments would reasonably have been understood by Sir Ben as a 'threat' of anything other than the claimant enforcing its legal rights to the fullest extent possible.

"Mr Nevin's words were intended to be, and would reasonably have been understood to be, used in a figurative rather than a literal sense."

Sports.title: Ex-Man City boss Roberto Mancini breaks silence on 115 charges verdict - 'Not my problem'
Sports.content:
Ex-Man City boss Roberto Mancini breaks silence on 115 charges verdict - 'Not my problem'

Roberto Mancini was appointed by Manchester City in 2009, the same year as the club's financial wrongdoing began, and he's alleged to have been paid off the books during his time as manager

View 2 Images Roberto Mancini has commented on the news (Image: Mustafa Yilmaz/Anadolu via Getty Images)

Roberto Mancini has attempted to distance himself from Manchester City's wrongdoing after they were found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial rules. The club, who strongly maintain their innocence, have been found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges brought against them back in 2023.

‌



City's breaches are alleged to have started in 2009 - the same year as Mancini took over - and ended in 2018. Among the allegations levelled against City are supposed payments made to Mancini off the books.

‌



The Italian, according to Gazzetta dello Sport, earned money from a second contract as well as another agreement with an Abu Dhabi club - Al Jazira - owned by City chief Sheikh Mansour worth £1.7million for a minimum of four days' consultancy per year. Mancini, however, insists that he isn't concerned about the allegations - and has a different opinion on the verdict.

‌



"I don't think Manchester City were found guilty, quite the opposite," the Italy manager said. "It's not a problem that concerns me, and it isn't anything new. Manchester City are not guilty, and on the double contract it isn't my problem, theirs if anything."

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

‌



Mancini was speaking ahead of Monday's Nations League clash with Turkey. The 61-year-old recently began his second spell as manager of Italy.

On Saturday, City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak told fans that he remains confident of proving the club's innocence. In a letter to supporters, Al Mubarak wrote: "Following Friday's media reporting, many of you will have spent your evening answering questions and responding to messages from friends, family and colleagues.

"So have I. Here's what I said to my family: The Premier League process still has a long way to run, and our confidence and intent in proving the Club's innocence is just as strong as when this began.

‌



What punishment should Manchester City receive? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Roberto Mancini led Manchester City to their first Premier League title (Image: Paul ELLIS/AFP via Getty Images)

"There are so many things that I would like to be able to share with you to help you understand why we feel so confident in our position. But the strict confidentiality of the legal process and our determination to respect it means I cannot do that at the moment. Even this letter underwent several legal checks to make sure it complies.

Article continues below

"I ask you to please carefully read the statement below, which we gave on Friday, and the statement we issued in February 2023. Every word matters and holds true.

"While some people have been quick to reach their own conclusions, and there is so much noise swirling around us, nothing has changed. We have faced challenges together before and have prevailed. There remain many who want to undermine the momentum of our Club. We will not give them that opportunity."

Sports.title: Roy Keane savages Cole Palmer and accuses star of 'bad habits' after England withdrawal
Sports.content:
Roy Keane savages Cole Palmer and accuses star of 'bad habits' after England withdrawal

Chelsea star Cole Palmer recently withdrew from the England squad because of a minor injury, sparking a debate over his future with the Three Lions under Thomas Tuchel

View 2 Images Roy Keane didn't mince his words (Image: ITV)

Roy Keane has told England fans to 'forget about' Cole Palmer taking them to another level, accusing him of having 'bad habits'. After missing out on the World Cup this summer, Chelsea star Palmer was recalled to Three Lions' squad by Thomas Tuchel but controversially pulled out because of a minor injury.

‌



Tuchel subsequently said that the 24-year-old 'misses too many camps' due to fitness problems. Ahead of England's 3-2 loss at home to Spain on Saturday, Keane weighed in on where Palmer's England career stands.

‌



"I think, whatever his injuries - and if he is injured - I watched his last game against Brentford and if you think he's going to get England to another level and win trophies, forget about it," the Manchester United legend declared on ITV. "I like Palmer, he's a talented boy, but he's got far too many bad habits for me."

‌



Tuchel called up Morgan Gibbs-White as a replacement for Palmer, who was one of five players to withdraw from the initial squad. Gibbs-White, 26, came on as a late substitute in the defeat to Spain and is expected to have the chance to impress during England's next three games.

But England aren't short of options in the No.10 role, as Tuchel said: "It leaves us with Jude Bellingham, Morgan Rogers, Morgan Gibbs-White and Eberechi Eze in that position.

"All in camp. All desperate to be here. All available. And all ready to go, ready to stop a holiday (like Gibbs-White) after one day in Dubai. I am not his friend. I am his national team coach and I can only judge him on what he is delivering for the national team and he is just missing too many opportunities."

The England manager went on to say: "My understanding is that Cole plays with discomfort and pain and he cannot compete on the highest level with discomfort and pain, so he withdrew and informed us and Chelsea informed us.

‌

"He misses too many opportunities, and I don't blame him for it. It's just the fact. He misses way too many camps with injuries and I only want to rely on what I personally witness and what I see within my team, and for that you have to be in camp.

Article continues below

"If you're not in camp, there's a next level to impress that you cannot achieve because you only can do it when you're actually with me on the pitch and with us on the pitch so, yeah, it is a missed opportunity.

"What sticks with me is the week that I have with the others. They (the absentees) lose that. That sticks. It sticks because we create something. We actually work off the field, on the field, about our principles, on how to be in. This brotherhood is so important and you miss out if you're not there."

Sports.title: Ireland players snub Israel handshakes and take action during national anthem before match
Sports.content:
Ireland players snub Israel handshakes and take action during national anthem before match

The Republic of Ireland faced Israel in the Nations League on Sunday evening, making a number of demonstrations ahead of kick-off due to the ongoing conflict in Gaza

View 2 Images Republic of Ireland players bowed their heads during the Israeli national anthem (Image: Attila KISBENEDEK / AFP via Getty Images)

Republic of Ireland players snubbed shaking hands with their Israeli opponents during Sunday evening's Nations League clash at the Nagyerdei Stadion. Heimir Hallgrimsson's men also bowed their heads during Israel's national anthem.

‌



It was a tense state of affairs as both sets of players made their way onto the pitch for the encounter, with no exchange of pennants. Captains, Dara O'Shea and Manor Solomon, also did not shake hands before or after the referee's coin toss to delegate kick-off and pitch sides.

‌



Ireland also made the decision to wear black armbands for the encounter, in recognition of the lives lost in the Gaza conflict. It comes as there were questions asked with regard to whether the match should have taken place at all, considering Israel's ongoing war with Palestine.

‌



Football Association of Ireland chief, David Courell told the press earlier this week that players held an intra-squad vote regarding their participation in the match against Israel, with a majority opting to go ahead. However, Gavin Bazunu withdrew himself from Hallgrimsson's squad on account of personal beliefs.

Ireland forced into unusual decision after squad split over controversial Israel match READ MORE :

Why Ireland players are wearing black armbands against Israel after player vote READ MORE :

Taking to Instagram, the Bolton Wanderers goalkeeper wrote: "My decision is based purely upon my personal belief that the killing of innocent people is wrong," adding: "It is important to note that my stance is not in opposition of the Israeli people or the Jewish community but against the atrocities in the region."

As a result of UEFA regulations for the competition, which stipulate that each squad must register at least three goalkeepers, Ireland made the decision to call up defender Jimmy Dunne to theoretically play backup to Caoimhin Kelleher and Max O'Leary - although the likelihood of him actually taking up a role in net is slim to none.

‌



Speaking about Ireland's decision to play Israel, Courell said: "The squad were in Pristina yesterday. An extensive conversation took place where ultimately the consensus from the group was to travel to Hungary.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

View 2 Images Gavin Bazunu pulled out of the fixture

‌



"That was something that we all entered into this window with our intention to fulfil these fixtures and that was the consensus that the group finished on at the end of that two-hour meeting yesterday. This morning a player (now confirmed to be Bazunu) expressed their discomfort with fulfilling this fixture to the head coach and indicated their intent to withdraw from the squad.

"As you can understand, this new variable required time and deliberation for the rest of the squad to consider. What proceeded was another four hours of conversations, predominantly amongst the players themselves but also at times with the coaching staff and at times with the executive.

"There was a lot of positions presented and I think it's important to say that from an association perspective and for everyone involved in those conversations, we were fully respectful of everyone's right to their respective opinion on these topics.

Article continues below

"Ultimately within the last maybe 90 minutes we carried out a vote amongst the squad to establish their sentiment on fulfilling the fixtures and it was a significant majority that was returned with the intention to continue."

Sports.title: James Trafford sends clear message to Jordan Pickford in battle to be England's undisputed No 1
Sports.content:
When Peter Shilton won his 125th and final cap for England - in the 1990 World Cup third-place play-off against Italy - he was 40 years old.

Jordan Pickford is 32. He has 91 England caps. Don’t think for one minute the Everton keeper does not have Shilton’s number in his mind.

Harry Kane will pass that mark fairly soon but Pickford will want to finish his international career as the most capped England keeper of all time. And he will want to set a number that looks unbeatable.

But now he knows he faces a battle to make that happen. James Trafford did not put in a show-stopping performance against Spain - three goals conceded tells that simple truth - but his selection was significant.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

In a way, it seems fair and understandable that Thomas Tuchel should split a four-game stretch into two games apiece for Pickford and Trafford. After all, being an unused understudy at a long World Cup is a thankless task. There was an element of reward in Trafford’s selection against Spain.

But this was a game - a competitive game - against Spain in front of a Wembley full house.

‌



Imagine Tuchel telling Harry Kane he had to sit this one out but would get a run in Croatia and against the Czech Republic back in London. Surely you play your best team against the world champions?

Maybe unfairly, this seemed like a shot across Pickford’s bows, a move that told him his position is no longer undisputed.

View 3 Images Trafford is now emerging as a serious rival to Jordan Pickford (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

And for someone who had just let in three goals, Trafford certainly exuded enough post-match confidence to suggest he fancies his chances of permanently deposing Pickford.

‌



He said: “I feel like I’ve had a great start to the season. The one thing I’m doing is playing and playing regularly and that’s one thing you have to do to get picked for your country.

“It’s every goalkeeper’s dream and every footballer’s dream to play for England and start for England. Everyone believes they can start and everyone’s just trying to prove every day that they can start.”

When he first took over, Tuchel made it clear that he wanted more competition for Pickford’s position but Trafford’s demotion to the Premier League bench at Manchester City effectively scuppered that prospect. But after his £40million move to Elland Road, Trafford can now go head-to-head with Pickford.

‌



He said: “Make no illusions. There are not many players who don’t play (in the Premier League) that start for any national team and it was always my aim to play in a top league and play for a top team in Leeds this season. That’s what I wanted to do.

“It’s an amazing club and I’ve loved every day that I’ve been there. It’s a great set of lads. I’m really happy.”

Trafford had returned to the Etihad as the obvious successor to Ederson but City then made a late-summer window move for Gianluigi Donnarumma and the ex-Burnley man was consigned to the domestic cup teams.

But he is not bitter, saying: “It obviously wasn’t ideal how it panned out but looking back, I got two trophies to my name, so you take the positives and you play the cards you’re dealt.”

‌



View 3 Images Pickford is closing in on Peter Shilton's record

And Trafford is being dealt another start by Tuchel in Prague on Tuesday night before Pickford takes over in Croatia and back at Wembley in a rematch with the Czech Republic.

But if this is some sort of head-to-head contest, Trafford is adamant it is a friendly one.

He said: “It’s the reality in football that everyone competes for the starting eleven. But me and Picks are northern lads and get along really well.”

‌

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel on collision course with Premier League bosses after blunt refusal
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel on collision course with Premier League bosses after blunt refusal

England players face a gruelling four games in 11 days, but Thomas Tuchel is adamant he will not listen to Premier League managers who ask for their stars to be rested

View 3 Images England manager Thomas Tuchel will not rest players during the international break (Image: Getty Images)

Thomas Tuchel will refuse to take any calls from Premier League managers - and insists it would be “madness” to expect him to rest players.

‌



Tuchel is ready to put himself on collision course with club bosses over England’s Nations League schedule as they face four games in the space of 11 days.

‌



England’s top stars came back from the World Cup exhausted, had short summer holidays and are straight back into a grueling fixture list with their clubs.

‌



But Tuchel insists he is determined to pick his strongest XI throughout the course of this international window even if Premier League clubs will be anxious about players getting injuries.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



England go straight from playing Spain at Wembley on Saturday to facing Czech Republic on Tuesday, Croatia next Saturday and then Czech Republic again at Wembley on Tuesday October 6.

England boss Tuchel said: “I don’t take calls from Premier League managers. I never called any national team coach. It is what it is.

“I cannot manage the players. It’s just impossible. I knew as a club coach – when I was on the other side – that I had this example many times.

‌



“If I would call a coach in Brazil or Argentina, they would not know what I am talking about. The players would not know what I am talking about.

View 3 Images England will play four games in 11 days

“So why would I do this and start giving the players the impression that it’s okay to take a step back or share a half or to rest one match? Why would I? I would never. It’s madness. We want to win the next match.”

‌



England had mass withdrawals before the squad met up with Declan Rice - who came to Wembley to support his England teammates - Cole Palmer, Tino Livramento, Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo all pulling out.

Morgan Gibbs-White and James Garner were called up and Tuchel does expect to make some changes through the run of fixtures but he will keep the core of the team which narrowly lost to Spain together.

Tuchel says that is his “ideal scenario” and has also suggested players may have to be subbed off early before getting into the dangerous territory when they are tired and fatigued at the end of games.

‌



View 3 Images England started their Nations League campaign with defeat to Spain

But Tuchel says he plans to play high intensity football against the Czech Republic - and there will be no let up in his demands.

Tuchel added: “Hopefully we can find that kind of shape and form but if you mean like ‘do we go for it and try to impose what we did today’ then yes that’s 100 per cent.

Article continues below

“We need to be proactive and go for it. There is no room for managing or an economic style. It’s how the team want to play, how we want to play so let’s go. It will be a different scenario and setting and a different challenge.”

Sports.title: Liverpool suffer another injury blow as Cody Gakpo hurt on international duty
Sports.content:
Liverpool suffer another injury blow as Cody Gakpo hurt on international duty

Cody Gakpo was forced off with an injury just 17 minutes into the Netherlands' clash with Serbia in the Nations League, providing Liverpool with another scare during the international break

View 2 Images Cody Gakpo has picked up an injury (Image: ANP via Getty Images)

Liverpool have been dealt a second injury blow in a matter of hours after Cody Gakpo had to be substituted for the Netherlands. Gakpo, 27, signalled to come off in the 17th minute of Sunday's game away to Serbia after being on the end of two strong challenges in quick succesion.

‌



The forward had scored for his country last time out to earn a 1-1 draw with Germany on Thursday, continuing a hot streak of form. But Gakpo's productive start to the season could be halted by the injury, having limped off the pitch during the Nations League fixture.

‌



Netherlands boss Xavi Hernandez is expected to provide an update at full-time. Earlier on Sunday, Liverpool discovered that Alexander Isak had picked up a thigh injury while playing for Sweden.

‌



The striker has now left Sweden's camp and will miss their three remaining matches. Although Liverpool don't return to action until October 11 against Manchester City, Reds boss Andoni Iraola will likely be sweating over his team selection already.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Gakpo and Isak have already combined for four goals this season, including their 1-0 win at Bournemouth prior to the international break. Sweden boss Graham Potter explained the nature of Isak's injury in a press conference before their match at home to Poland on Monday.

"He's got a small problem with his thigh," Potter said. "It's not a big one but because of the amount of games we've got in a small space of time, he won't be able to make those.

"Not a big one but it's frustrating for him and obviously for us. It is what it is but we move forward with the players we have.

‌



"It was during the game. Like anything, you sometimes get bumps and bruises in the game, you might think it's a bit of a dead leg or something. But actually as the 24 hours, 48 hours after the game, not quite what you think.

How should Liverpool line up if Cody Gakpo and Alexander Isak are missing? Let us know your XI in the comments section.

View 2 Images Cody Gakpo was tackled by Serbia's Sasa Lukic (Image: Roy Lazet/Soccrates/Getty Images)

‌



"Unfortunately after getting it checked out, it's a little bit more than what you think during the match. He has to miss the rest of the camp.

"Our medical team has been in contact with the club. Obviously it's our decision in the first place because of his status, in terms of his injury. Once that's the case, we have to inform everybody. That's just normal.

"We've got a really big squad that we believe in. Clearly there's not another Alexander Isak, that's obvious.

Article continues below

"In an ideal world, we want all our players available but the reality is we don't have Alex for this game… clearly whoever comes in, we're not going to ask them to be Alex. They just need to be themselves in the best way they can."

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland beat Israel in controversial Nations League meeting
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in their controversial Nations League fixture at a neutral venue in Hungary.

Players did not shake hands with each other before their meeting at the Nagyerdei Stadion in Debrecen and there was no exchange between Ireland captain Dara O'Shea and Israel's Manor Solomon.

Ireland players also appeared to bow their heads while Israel's national anthem was played out before kick-off.

Black armbands were worn by Ireland players, which Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chief executive David Courell said was a gesture to recognise "all lives lost" in the Israel-Gaza conflict.

Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu was the only player who chose not to play after the squad voted to proceed with the match on Saturday amid calls for the game not to go ahead.

Goals from Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan sealed the victory for Heimir Hallgrimsson's side.

Moylan celebrated his goal by kissing and raising his black armband before kissing his badge.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland slip to deserved defeat in Kosovo
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland slipped to a 1-0 defeat away to Kosovo in their Nations League opener in Pristina.

The build-up to the League B3 encounter had been overshadowed by the controversy around upcoming fixtures against Israel, which Republic boss Heimir Hallgrimsson had admitted many of his squad members were uncomfortable about playing.

Chiedozie Ogbene had fired an early chance over before Kosovo responded to finish the first half strongly at the Fadil Vokrri Stadium.

The home side saw two shots cleared off the line and Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher then clawed away a header from Vedat Muriqi as Hallgrimsson's side got to the break on level terms.

Ireland - who are scheduled to play Israel in Hungary on Sunday and then again in a 'home' tie at another neutral venue in Serbia seven days later - dug in for the second half but were eventually undone with seven minutes left when Kosovo captain Muriqi bundled the ball in from close range.

Udinese defender James Abankwah was handed a first competitive start as part of a back five, with in-form Real Betis striker Troy Parrott the lone forward and Dara O'Shea taking the captain's armband.

Image: The Republic of Ireland have won two of their six games in 2026 so far

Ireland created what ended up being their only real clear chance in the 22nd minute. Abankwah got away down the right and ran into the Kosovo penalty area before cutting the ball back to Ogbene, who sent a curling effort over the crossbar.

Kosovo, who are in League B for the first time, went close on the half-hour mark when a cross from the left found its way through to Muriqi, whose angled shot was cleared off the line by Jayson Molumby.

Veldin Hodza then saw his 10-yard strike blocked in front of goal by O'Shea before Kelleher got up to claw away a looping header from Muriqi, which was set for the top corner.

Ireland made a positive start to the second half, with a deep cross from the right by Abankwah finding Parrott at the far post and his header was gathered by Kosovo goalkeeper Arijanet Muric.

Image: Vedat Muriqi scored the winner for Kosovo

Kosovo, though, continued to carry a threat themselves. Baton Zabergja sent a 20-yard effort just wide of the top corner, which again got the home supporters into full voice.

Muriqi forced Kelleher into another smart reaction save from an angled shot at the near post before Kosovo eventually made the breakthrough in the 83rd minute.

Ermal Krasniqi's shot was deflected onto the crossbar and Muriqi reacted quickest in a crowded six-yard box to nod the ball over the line.

Kosovo should have got a second late on when substitute Krasniqi dragged his shot wide after being set up by Muriqi following a break onto a long ball.

Ireland pay price for 'off day'

Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson told RTE:

"[Kosovo are] a good team, momentum with them, crowd with them, and to be honest they deserve the win.

"There was nothing that we didn't know about how they would play, where their threats would be, but [it was] an off day for a lot of our players and [it is] a tough place to come to if you have an off day, so a deserved win for Kosovo."

Hallgrimsson added: "We were the team that needed to defend today and didn't connect in possession or passes, not as sharp as we have done.

"We have to quickly find out the reason that we had an off day. We can all do better than we did today.

"It is a two-day turnaround for the next one, so we better be quick…and do better than this versus Israel. They are probably in the same position as us [having lost to Austria]."

Asked if the controversy from playing the fixtures against Israel had impacted on his team's performance against Kosovo, Hallgrimsson said: "I couldn't say now. It is difficult to measure that one."

He added: "This is the situation, we have to cope with it. And like I said before the game, this camp is a test of character.

"We need to do better in that area than we did here today. We knew that we needed to win the duels, win the one-vs-ones, but sadly they had the upper hand on all the basics."

What it means and next fixtures

Sports.title: Why have the Republic of Ireland's two games against Israel become so controversial?
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland will face Israel in a men’s football fixture for the first time since 2005 in this international break, but there have been calls for the two UEFA Nations League games not to be played at all.

Both meetings - the first played in Debrecen, Hungary on Sunday and the second scheduled for the Serbian town of Backa Topola on October 4 - have been overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

Uncertainty over the games going ahead might have subsided, but the tensions between the two nations have not.

Heimir Hallgrimsson, the Republic of Ireland head coach, has been accused of "stupidity and hypocrisy" by the Israel Football Association after last week suggesting his team would be "playing against genocide" when facing Israel, while his players are not ruling out their own protests ahead of the games.

The Athletic examines the key issues ahead of the first meeting this weekend.

Why have these games caused controversy?

This has been a contentious issue rolling down the tracks ever since the 2026-27 Nations League draw was made in February. Group B3 saw the Republic of Ireland pitted against Kosovo, their opening opponents this evening, and Austria, but it was the prospect of facing Israel which created immediate unease.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) had overwhelmingly approved a motion that called on UEFA to ban Israel from its competitions just four months earlier due to violations of the governing body's statutes, including "the organisation of clubs in illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank without the consent of the Palestinian Football Association".

The Nations League draw duly reignited the row. Irish politicians, including the FAI member Joanna Byrne, were quick to call for a boycott of the Israel games in the following days and protests ensued when Qatar visited Dublin's Aviva Stadium for a friendly in May. Tennis balls featuring the Palestine flag were thrown on the pitch by supporters, twice causing brief interruptions.

Image: Tennis balls with a Palestinian flag on were thrown onto the pitch in Dublin during protests in May 2026

The FAI had already confirmed its plans to go ahead with the Israel games by then, and that decision was formally approved at an EGM in July.

That saw only 32 votes in favour of a boycott, with 75 members voting for the games to be played. The FAI had argued that boycotting games would cause "significant and lasting harm to Irish football" due to the likely disciplinary sanctions from UEFA.

A measure of the opposition to the Republic of Ireland facing Israel also came with the acceptance that the "home" fixture would not be played in Dublin. The FAI cited "operational challenges (that) could impact the delivery of the game on home soil" and the decision was eventually made in late June, with the support of UEFA, to move the game to Backa Topola, a small town in northern Serbia, on Sunday week.

No tickets for the game will be made available to Ireland fans.

The FAI has subsequently revealed that a request to see the two nations kept apart in future competition draws has been rejected by UEFA.

"The answer I got was very clear," FAI chief executive David Courell told reporters on September 18. "That would not be possible because Ireland and Israel have never been in direct conflict."

What is the political backdrop?

The Republic of Ireland has consistently outlined its backing for the Palestinian people since the conflict with Israel began almost three years ago, joining Norway and Spain when officially recognising a Palestinian state in 2024. Taoiseach Micheal Martin has also made his stance clear, accusing Israel of committing "genocide" last year in comments reported by the Irish Mirror.

The conflict in Gaza began after Israel responded to attacks by Hamas militants on October 7, 2023, which saw around 1,200 people, mostly civilians, killed in Israel and 250 taken hostage. The war has subsequently seen 73,000 people killed, according to figures from the Gaza Health Ministry and used by the UN.

Strained relations between the Republic of Ireland and Israel have continued this year. Two Israeli government ministers were the subject of travel bans in June, while foreign minister Helen McEntee also confirmed Ireland's intent to limit goods trading with settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank this summer.

Image: Taoiseach Micheal Martin

A meeting between the Republic of Ireland and Israel on a football field this weekend has subsequently taken on enormous significance against such a backdrop.

There are similarities in Ireland's political stance with those of Norway, who faced similar calls for a boycott when Israel travelled to Oslo last October. The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) had aligned itself with its government and said in a statement leading up to Israel's visit that the "tragic humanitarian suffering in Gaza" had made the fixture challenging.

That World Cup qualifier, won 5-0 by Norway, saw thousands take part in a protest march to the stadium.

Who has opposed the games taking place?

Moving a home game 1,500 miles away has not stopped the objections building ahead of the two teams meeting on Sunday. More than 160 Irish sportspeople signed an open letter asking their national team to boycott the Israel games under the banner of the Irish Sport for Palestine Group, who have also run the "Stop the Game" campaign that protested outside of the Irish team hotel in Dublin on Monday.

"This is a significant moment and with this moment you have an opportunity to do the right thing," the letter said.

Kevin Kilbane, the former Republic of Ireland international who holds 110 caps, has also been unequivocal in his views. "The Republic of Ireland should not be playing Israel… not while Israeli forces are committing genocide," he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.">he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.

Amnesty International also issued a fresh statement on Tuesday that said UEFA risked letting football "rubber-stamp apartheid" by allowing Israel's continued participation in its club and international competitions. A spokesperson for the Israeli FA responded to that by saying: "Their obsession with the idea of Israel as a state is incurable, as is their need of attention."

The Irish media, meanwhile, has faced its own dilemmas in the coverage of the Israel games. RTE, the public broadcaster behind Ireland's boycott of the Eurovision Song Contest in the last two years due to Israel's continued involvement, has stripped back its coverage. Contractual obligations will be met, RTE confirmed in a statement, but there would be no studio coverage or commentators sent to either fixture.

Image: Kevin Kilbane, former Ireland international, has spoken out

What have the key stakeholders said ahead of this weekend?

Relations between the two nations have grown increasingly hostile in the last week. Hallgrimsson appeared in front of the media to announce his squad for the upcoming friendlies and made pointed remarks when asked how his players would focus on football.

"We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide," the former Iceland head coach told reporters. "We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."

The reaction to those words, in a social media post from the Israel FA account, raised temperatures further still. "We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way," it read. "Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them."

Martin, who was among the world leaders attending the UN General Assembly in New York, was then drawn back into debate on Tuesday. "I think those are unacceptable remarks. They should be withdrawn. Israel can't keep denying what the world knows and what the world understands."

The FAI has not addressed Hallgrimsson's comments publicly, but the Republic of Ireland's head coach said on Wednesday that he had been "grateful for the support" he had received.

"Maybe from a leadership point of view, it was not clever from me to take the attention (away) like this. It's a tricky time for us," Hallgrimsson said in his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Kosovo.

The same extends to his players, too. Dara O'Shea, the Ipswich Town defender, said, according to the BBC, that he and the rest of the players would come together on Friday to "openly discuss" the prospect of a protest ahead of the first Israel game in Debrecen on Sunday.

Image: Dara O’Shea, left, and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson during Wednesday’s press conference

Why are the games being played in Hungary and Serbia?

Hungary has acted as an adopted home for Israel since the start of the conflict. They first played there in November 2023, when resuming their attempts to qualify for Euro 2024 when hosting Switzerland at the Pancho Arena in Felcsut, a small village 26 miles west of Budapest.

Victor Orban, who lost his position as Hungary's prime minister this year, had been a long-standing ally of Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and claimed Hungary to be the "safest country in Europe" for Jews.

The World Cup 2026 qualifiers against Estonia, Norway and Italy were all held in Debrecen, which has also previously hosted European games for Israeli sides Maccabi Haifa and Maccabi Tel Aviv.

The Republic of Ireland's choice of Backa Topola, Serbia, is less clear. Dublin ceased to become an option, even behind closed doors, as the opposition to Israel visiting became clear, which left limited options for relocation.

It needed to be a nation sympathetic to Israel to avoid further protests and Serbia, neighbouring Hungary to the south, has forged strong diplomatic relations. According to the Associated Press, Serbia's president Aleksandar Vucic inaugurated an assembly factory for Israel-made drones last week, with plans for three more production sites.

A switch to Serbia was reliant on UEFA approval and it will be Backa Topola's home of the TSC Arena where this story ends on October 4.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
