World.title: Houston Astros secure the most embarrassing kind of Major League Baseball history with AL West win
World.content:
When Major League Baseball changed the schedule to ensure that the final day of the regular season featured all 15 games starting within a few minutes of each other, Sunday is what they envisioned. Mostly.

While most postseason spots and seeds were decided either within the last week or the last few days, there were two races that came down to the final day of the year. The American League West race featured the Houston Astros and Texas Rangers entering the day tied at 80-81, remarkably, and the third wild card spot in the National League between the Philadelphia Phillies and Arizona Diamondbacks.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

The Phillies, who as recently as last week had a 99.1% chance of reaching the postseason, per FanGraphs, avoided a historic collapse and clinched a wild card series appearance with a 7-3 win over the Tampa Bay Rays.

WITH ONE MONTH LEFT, AMERICAN LEAGUE TEAMS ARE HEADING TOWARDS AN EMBARRASSING, HISTORIC LOW

But the Astros, even with a win, did in fact make an embarrassing type of history: they are officially the worst division-winning team in baseball history.

The previous low-water mark was the 2005 San Diego Padres, who won the NL West with an 82-80 record. And while the Astros won 9-0 over the long-eliminated Athletics to avoid the 80-82 record, 81–81 marks a new low winning percentage for a division winner over a full season.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Even crazier? The Astros were extremely fortunate to finish the season at .500.

While wins and losses are what decide the standings and outcomes, run differential has proven over time to be a significantly better predictor of future win and loss records than the previous standings. Essentially, the better you are at outscoring the opposition, the more likely it is that you'll win more games moving forward. One-run outcomes are not sustainable, but blowouts are illustrative of team quality.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Run differentials are also used to build "expected" records. Meaning that in the history of baseball, a specific run differential is expected to result in a given number of wins and losses. The Miami Marlins, for example, outscored the opposition by just three runs over the course of the season, which is an "expected" record of 81-81. Makes sense, they were even with the other teams in the league, they should finish at an even .500.



By contrast, the Milwaukee Brewers finished with a league-best +214 run differential, good for an "expected" record of 103-59. They finished 103-59.

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

But teams frequently over perform or underperform against their expected win-loss record, for any number of reasons. A bad bullpen could mean a team wins blowouts, but loses more than their fair share of close games. Bad luck. Poorly timed injuries. Poor defense. Inconsistent hitting with runners in scoring position. The randomness of baseball. Or a dominant closer who shuts the door consistently in close games.

This year's 81-81 division winning Astros team was so bad they were outscored 32 runs over the course of the season, good for just an 78-84 expected win-loss record. While the Rangers and their fans are sure to be disappointed with the outcome, missing out on the final day, they were even worse. Texas had a -46 run differential, and a 76-86 expected record.

These are not good baseball teams.

So it's a near-certainty that Houston will make a quick postseason exit, right?

Yeah, no, not at all. Houston plays the Chicago White Sox in the best-of-three wild card series, which the Astros now host as division winners. Chicago's a better team, but the randomness inherent in the small sample size of a playoff series makes the result effectively a toss up. In fact, FanGraphs gives the Astros a 55% chance of advancing to the ALDS.

Should Houston win that series, they'd play the extremely mediocre Cleveland Guardians, who finished with a +11 run differential and 85-77 record. Cleveland may be slight favorites in that series, maybe 57-43, but hardly a foregone conclusion. Which means we could be staring down the barrel of an 81-81 team reaching the ALCS.

MLB always hoped for last-minute drama by starting every game around the same time on the final day of the regular season. They got it.

They also got the worst-ever division winning team because the league's financial incentives and playoff structure encourage owners to do the bare minimum and spend as little as possible to win 85 games and hope for the best. Or in Houston's case, 81. The Astros benefited, and fans were forced to watch the AL West "battle" lost.

World.title: Foiled terror plot at bomber base signals wider threat to US military installations: expert
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Five men arrested near a key U.S. bomber base in the U.K. on Sunday may have planned a "complex," coordinated attack with potentially far-reaching security implications for American military installations globally, a former U.S. intelligence official warned.

As counterterrorism police investigated after officers detained the suspects near RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire, a former Pentagon official also said President Donald Trump will ultimately be the one to decide the consequences if indeed the "trail leads to Tehran."

The men were initially held on suspicion of offenses under Britain’s Explosives Act before being arrested on terrorism charges in connection with the airfield, a key U.S. Air Force hub and the primary European base for American strategic bombers.

On Sunday, Trump said U.S. authorities had been monitoring the suspects prior to their capture.

FORMER UK PRIME MINISTER TONY BLAIR WARNS EUROPE ‘WE DON’T WIN’ IN WAR WITHOUT US SUPPORT

"We had them under investigation," Trump told reporters in Chicago. "They were looking to do big damage to our fort."

"It may have been Scotland Yard. I don't know. We worked with a lot of them. We had them under view for a long time, and we got them," Trump added.

According to Sky News, counterterrorism police were investigating whether Iran is linked to the suspected bomb plot.

Former Trump White House official Morgan Murphy told Fox News Digital that British authorities are leading the investigation alongside U.S. law enforcement and intelligence.

"Every phone, bank record and rental receipt will be run through British and American intelligence, and if the trail leads to Tehran, it will be found," Murphy clarified.

"But as American airmen and bombers seem to have been the target, Air Force investigators on the base, the FBI in London, and American intelligence will likely all work the case."

"If conclusive evidence proves Iran is behind an attempted attack on U.S. forces, the American President will ultimately decide how Tehran pays," Murphy added.

BRITAIN INTRODUCES SWEEPING NEW POWERS TO TARGET FOREIGN STATE-LINKED GROUPS INCLUDING IRAN'S IRGC

Former Defense Intelligence Agency official Andrew Badger told Fox News Digital the number of suspects and vehicles involved raised the possibility of a sophisticated operation.

"We are going to see elevated security protocols across Europe, across the U.K., and across the entire world for any U.S. installation," he said.

"This is a very significant threat, and again, seeing that we had five individuals involved and three different reported vans at the scene, this could have been a very complex, highly orchestrated operation," Badger added.

"This isn't just some type of amateur lone wolf operation," he said, noting Fairford’s strategic importance to the U.S. military. "Fairford is also where the U.S. houses its strategic bombers for Europe as well as the rest of the world."

He said a potential attack posed broader risks beyond the airfield itself which he said "could have had significant security implications. It could have damaged the nearby area."

HOW IRAN ATTACKS ARE FORCING THE PENTAGON TO RETHINK ITS DECADES-OLD MIDDLE EAST BASE STRATEGY

"They could have tried to use a VBIED or a vehicle-borne explosive device where the first van could have gone off at the front gate, and then the other vans would have gone in and tried to go for the strategic bombers," Badger said.

British authorities have not publicly identified who they believe was behind the suspected plot or announced a motive, but RAF Fairford had taken on greater strategic importance during the war with Iran.

The U.K. government previously authorized U.S. forces to use the Royal Air Force bases Fairford and Diego Garcia for limited defensive operations, including destroying Iranian missiles and launchers at their source.

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) later warned that any base used to attack Iranian territory would be considered a legitimate target.

"Any base used to launch attacks on Iranian territory is a legitimate target for our forces," the IRGC said, according to reports.

"Tehran warned London in July to keep American bombers off Fairford, and if this plot traces back to Iran, the answer must be more bombers, not fewer," Morgan said.

IRAN EXPERT BRANDS ISLAMIC CENTER OF ENGLAND IRAN'S 'UK OFFICE,' URGES IMMEDIATE CLOSURE

A local councilor told Reuters there had been a recent security alert at Fairford and surveillance had been stepped up.

"So there was a specific threat about six weeks ago from the Iranians on this base. At the time, there was increased surveillance around the area," he told the outlet.

Badger, however, cautioned against assuming Iran was responsible while pointing to other potential threats.

"This could be Iran trying to gain strategic leverage in negotiations, but there are other actors as well," Badger added.

"But there's Russia, who's been launching a campaign of gray zone or hybrid warfare attacks across Europe, as well as Islamic extremists, which are still a significant threat here in the U.K."

"Was this some type of retaliation by Iran to perhaps try to gain leverage or to try to inflict a cost for the U.S. withdrawing from these negotiations? Again, we don't know for sure, but it is a possibility," Badger said.

Badger also pointed to RAF Welford, a major U.S. ammunition storage facility that primarily supports operations at RAF Fairford.

US EMBASSIES IN MIDDLE EAST WARN AMERICANS OF 'UNFORESEEN ESCALATION' AS LATEST STRIKES HIT IRAN

"RAF Welford is actually the second-largest weapons and ammunition depot in all of Europe," Badger said, noting that the facility where the U.S. stores ammunition "could have been a target as well."

"Other bases across Europe, including European and U.S. partners, have already been on a heightened state of alert," Badger continued.

"But of course, after this attack, I think they're going to be in an even more heightened state. You're going to have more frequent security patrols."

"There are reports that RAF Fairford was put onto what's called the Delta alert, which is the highest state of security alert within the military base system," Badger said.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

"So this is basically that 'an imminent terrorist attack is inbound,'" he concluded.

World.title: Angels reach historic 100-loss low with season-closing defeat against Mariners as new era looms
World.content:
A season worth forgetting in Anaheim ended with a mark that will linger in baseball history forever.

With a 7-3 loss to the Seattle Mariners at T-Mobile Park on Sunday, the Los Angeles Angels (62-100) officially crossed a threshold they had evaded for 65 years: their first 100-loss season.

The defeat stripped the Halos of their standing as the last MLB franchise to avoid triple-digit losses, putting all 30 clubs on the century-mark ledger.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

For first-year manager Kurt Suzuki, Game 162 was the grim culmination of a grueling campaign, one that ultimately eclipsed the 63-99 mark set by Ron Washington’s 2024 squad.

The finale carried an unmistakable layer of drama. Franchise star Mike Trout watched from the dugout on a scheduled day off as his young teammates fought to avert history.

Shortstop Zach Neto had insisted earlier in the week that organizational pride would propel them past the brink, and a 5-4 stretch in their final nine games gave Anaheim a flicker of hope. But Sunday proved unforgiving.

ANGELS SEEM COMPLETELY UNAWARE THEY ARE THE WORST TEAM IN MLB: 'OUR BEST BASEBALL IS AHEAD OF US'

Former Mariner Yusei Kikuchi (1-7) was tagged early by his old club, surrendering three runs over five innings. After Angels' Bryce Teodosio trimmed the deficit to 3-1 with a sixth-inning sacrifice fly, Seattle quickly slammed the door. A costly throwing error and a two-run double by Randy Arozarena pushed the margin out of reach. A late solo shot by Jose Siri provided a brief spark, but the season expired when Dominic Canzone squeezed a fly ball off the bat of Christian Moore for the final out.

Following the June 26 firing of GM Perry Minasian, interim GM John Mozeliak tore down the roster, shipping out fan favorites Taylor Ward, Jo Adell, Logan O'Hoppe and Chase Silseth (and more) for prospects and leaving Suzuki with a stripped-down, youthful core down the stretch.



Yet, hitting rock bottom arrives with a sudden shift in momentum.

The end of Arte Moreno's era is officially underway following an agreement to sell the controlling interest of the franchise to Stan Kroenke’s group for a record $4 billion.

For a fanbase enduring its lowest historical point, Kroenke’s proven track record of constructing championship rosters across professional sports offers what Anaheim has lacked for decades: a real vision forward.

World.title: Trevor Lawrence fantasy owners are beside themselves after inexplicable decision in fourth quarter blowout
World.content:
Life is pretty sweet if you're a Jacksonville Jaguars fan as of late.

Last year, the Jags went 13-4, their best season since 1999, and sit atop the AFC South three games into this season with one of the best coach-quarterback combos in the NFL.

Duval's finest absolutely crushed last year's AFC Champions, the New England Patriots, thanks in large part to the play of that aforementioned quarterback.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

JACKSONVILLE JAGUARS SET AT 8.5 WIN TOTAL AFTER SURPRISING 13-4 SEASON AND WILD CARD LOSS TO BUFFALO

Trevor Lawrence tossed three touchdowns in a blowout 35-6 victory on Sunday, but he could have added a rushing touchdown midway through the fourth quarter as well.

With the Jaguars leading 28-6 with just under nine minutes left in the game, Lawrence took a designed quarterback keeper on third and three and broke into the clear.

NFL'S DUMBEST MOMENT OF WEEK 2 GOES TO JETS COACH AARON GLENN WHO PLAYED NOT TO LOSE AT END OF REGULATION

Then the flaxen-maned signal caller did something pretty inexplicable by all accounts: he slid at the one-yard line.

Okay, analytics nerds, I'm ready for any and all explanations on this one.

I get that you want to burn as much time as possible when you're holding a lead, but a touchdown there gives you a four-score lead with just over half a quarter left in the game.

The Patriots looked downright anemic on offense, mustering two field goals the entire game, and even if they somehow miraculously found the end zone four times in the next eight minutes, they still would've needed at least one two-point conversion just to tie the ballgame.

So again, I ask, what's the thought process here.

I've never been one to get too up in arms when it comes to things like this, but luckily the internet did it for me, as a bunch of angry fantasy football owners and amateur gamblers were ready to throw their phones through a wall after this one.

RAIDERS STAR BROCK BOWERS SHOCKINGLY UNDERGOES MENISCUS TRIM SURGERY AS FANTASY MANAGERS FUME AHEAD OF WEEK 1

I don't get the move, but I certainly don't think there's anything nefarious going on here.

Lawrence likely wanted to burn as much time as possible, and although I think it was ultimately a pointless endeavor, I can understand the logic.

I would say to put your tinfoil hats away, folks, but Lawrence actually gave a tongue-in-cheek answer about it when speaking during his postgame interview

World.title: Kathy Griffin says Ed Sheeran should have told Robert Kraft to 'go f--- yourself' over Macklemore
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Comedian Kathy Griffin said on Wednesday that singer Ed Sheeran should have told Gillette Stadium owner and billionaire Robert Kraft to "go f--- yourself" after barring Macklemore from performing as his opening act over his "Free Palestine" stunt.

In an interview with Queerty, Griffin commented on Macklemore being pulled from the rest of Sheeran's tour earlier this month after he repeatedly pushed for a "Free Palestine" during his act and performed his anti-Israel song "Hind's Hall." The decision came after Kraft barred Macklemore from performing at Gillette Stadium.

Though Sheeran has said that the decision ultimately came from the concert promoter and venues rather than him, Griffin argued that Sheeran could have, and should have, defended Macklemore at the time.

MACKLEMORE'S LONG HISTORY OF CONTROVERSY FROM GRAMMY WINS TO 'FREE PALESTINE' CONCERT REMARKS

"I wish that Ed Sheeran had not taken the advice of the ones who told him to fire Macklemore," Griffin said. "Let’s not be listening to f------ Robert Kraft. When Robert Kraft says I’ve called all the other stadium owners and they’re not gonna let you do the show with Macklemore either, Ed Sheeran should’ve said go f--- yourself, I can go to Brazil and perform for 250,000 people. He had more options."

Griffin added that Macklemore's comments were protected under the First Amendment and professed her own support for a "Free Palestine."

"I don't think 'Free Palestine' is such a controversial thing to say because that's a genuine genocide that is happening there, in my opinion. I don't want Israel to be eradicated. I love the Israeli people as I hope the rest of the world likes the American people but hates [President Donald] Trump and his cabinet and our current SCOTUS. So I can't stand [Israeli Prime Minister] Bibi Netanyahu. I think he's ruined the Knesset which is their Congress. But I certainly don't have a beef with the Jewish people or the Palestinian people. They're both trying to survive. I personally think that Palestine should be its own country," Griffin said.

ROBERT KRAFT PLEDGES $2M FOR HUMANITARIAN AID AS MACKLEMORE FACES FALLOUT OVER VENUE BAN

Fox News Digital reached out to Sheeran's and Kraft's representatives for comment.

In response to being removed from Sheeran's tour, Macklemore announced on Thursday that he would be launching his own "Free Palestine Tour." As of now, he has three shows scheduled: in Dublin on Oct. 26, in Paris on Oct. 29 and in London on Oct. 30.

Though Macklemore has received support from progressive figures for his political actions, the singer has also faced criticism from pro-Israel organizations who accused him of supporting antisemitism.

MACKLEMORE BAN BY ROBERT KRAFT DRAWS FIRE FROM AOC AND CAIR WHO ADVOCATE FOR FREE SPEECH ONLY WHEN CONVENIENT

The Israeli-American Council (IAC) released a statement to Fox News Digital supporting Kraft's actions pushing back against Macklemore.

"The Israeli-American Council (IAC) applauds Robert Kraft and his fellow stadium owners for their moral leadership in expelling rapper Macklemore from the concert stage rather than allow him to promote antisemitism," the statement read.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

It added, "Robert Kraft's moral leadership establishes what should be an obvious principle: a performer who traffics in antisemitism should not be given a stage. As a result, Macklemore will no longer be allowed to subject audiences to his hateful rants. The IAC salutes and thanks Mr. Kraft for setting an example for all to follow."

Fox News' Emily Trainham contributed to this report.

World.title: Baker Mayfield leaves game after writhing in pain on turf in Tampa Bay when thumb on throwing hand injured
World.content:
Baker Mayfield was trying to lead a fourth-quarterback comeback against the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday when he found himself heaving a desperation fourth-down pass which got intercepted. And then something really bad happened.

As Vikings linebacker Andrew Van Ginkel was cradling the interception, back up field Mayfield was on the ground literally screaming in pain.

He clearly injured the thumb on his throwing hand.

His THROWING hand, folks.

The finger bent in a manner it should not.

After the game, Bucs head coach Todd Bowles announced Mayfield suffered a dislocated thumb.

"He'll get an MRI tomorrow just to see exactly what inside is wrong," Bowles said. "We'll know more tomorrow."

The "know more" part will determine how much rather than if Mayfield suffered ligament damage. The tests will also determine if Mayfield will need surgery.

If Mayfield needs surgery, he's probably looking at a stint on the injured reserve list, which would require him to miss four games.

His return to play will be determined by how long it eventually takes him to regain his grip.

World.title: Here’s the biggest news you missed this weekend
World.content:
A powerful nor’easter battered the Northeast again on Sunday, flooding coastal communities and leaving tens of thousands of homes and businesses without power as forecasters warned that another round of high tides could inundate vulnerable shorelines.

The slow-moving storm, which killed a New York City Housing Authority worker when a tree fell Saturday, was expected to linger through Sunday with heavy rain, strong winds and dangerous surf from New Jersey to New England.

The nor’easter triggered memories of Superstorm Sandy, which left behind over $60 billion in damage across the eastern U.S. in 2012. While this storm’s impact has been nowhere near that, it could be the first of several along the East Coast this fall because of an El Niño climate pattern that’s disrupting this year’s weather.

Hurricane Nolo skirts Hawaii, but powerful winds and flooding remain threats

Hilo, Hawaii, on Saturday before Hurricane Nolo approaches. Gregory Bull / AP

Officials said Hurricane Nolo still posed a risk for flash floods, dangerous winds and extreme surf in areas recovering from previous storms.

Nolo was churning very slowly south of the Big Island with maximum sustained winds of 90 mph. Its center was about 165 miles south-southwest of Hawaii’s southernmost point, and it was forecast to strengthen into a major hurricane late Sunday and early Monday while traveling westward to the south of the islands.

Five men arrested on terrorism charge near U.S. air base in Britain

A B-1 bomber at RAF Fairford in England on July 25. Matthew Horwood / Getty Images

British police arrested several men on suspicion of terrorism and explosives offenses on Sunday and evacuated homes near an air base that the U.S. Air Force had been using to facilitate strikes on Iran.

A major incident was declared, with a massive emergency presence seen around RAF Fairford, which is about 90 minutes outside London, close to the village of Whelford in west England.

The Gloucestershire police force said it responded in the early hours of Sunday to reports of three suspicious vehicles moving toward the base and arrested five men.

Asked about the incident, President Donald Trump told reporters the arrest was an “amazing job.”

Iran ‘fully prepared’ for war to resume, but diplomacy not over yet, foreign minister says

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said his country is prepared to resume fighting with the United States but has not yet abandoned diplomacy after Trump publicly rejected a proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

“We are fully prepared for the war to be resumed. We stand firm in the face of any new aggression, even if it comes to a doomsday war,” Araghchi told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” on Sunday, when asked about a Wall Street Journal report that Trump could seek to resume bombing after the U.S. midterm elections. “At the same time, we stand ready for diplomacy. It is up to President Trump to choose.”

Araghchi told moderator Kristen Welker that despite Trump’s public comments, the rejection had still not been officially communicated to Iran via mediators.

He reaffirmed that Iran was ready to reopen the strait as part of an agreement to end the conflict, adding that in return, “we want our monies, our assets, which are illegally frozen, to be released. We want to be able to sell our oil.”

Bill Gates says getting global AI regulations will be harder than Cold War-era nuclear negotiations

Microsoft co-founder and billionaire philanthropist Bill Gates called on the U.S. to be a leader in regulating the growth of artificial intelligence but warned that getting countries to agree on a global framework could be “more difficult” than Cold War-era negotiations to limit nuclear weapons.

“This is more difficult than that was,” Gates told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” on Wednesday during a wide-ranging discussion on AI that aired Sunday.

His remarks came as he spoke about Trump’s stance against regulating AI. Gates argued that regulating AI companies by imposing monitoring systems would not hamper the U.S. in any race with China to develop superior technology.

In a Sunday interview on “Meet the Press,” Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., said the U.S. and China need to form a working group with technology experts from both countries to come to an agreement on AI.

Some lawmakers doubt a Congress that’s ‘barely capable of email’ can regulate AI

“A lot of them can’t spell it,” quipped GOP Sen. Thom Tillis. Democratic Sen. Ruben Gallego was equally skeptical: “They still don’t know how to get on the internet.”

One thing that everyone seems to agree on: Congress is not close to regulating AI. It hasn’t passed any sweeping, comprehensive legislation regulating the internet, invented more than 40 years ago, instead taking a more piecemeal approach and relying on existing laws.

New York Knicks’ Jalen Brunson kicks off the new season of ‘SNL’

Host Jalen Brunson and Marcello Hernández, center, with musical guest Katseye during "Saturday Night Live" promos last week. Rosalind O'Connor / NBC

NBA Finals MVP Jalen Brunson, of the 2026 championship-winning New York Knicks, kicked off the 52nd season of “Saturday Night Live” with musical guest Katseye.

Brunson delivered a monologue in which he promised to approach his “SNL” performance with the same strategy he used during Knicks’ NBA Finals games.

“The first three quarters of the show are going to be god-awful,” he said. “The last sketch is going to be amazing.”

Saturday’s show also marked the first “SNL” season for two new featured players, Saidah Belo-Osagie and Grace Reiter, after it bid farewell to cast member Chloe Fineman and writer Martin Herlihy.

Notable quote

It’s as if I’m living with a machete at the back of my neck, ready to be chopped off at any moment. Maricarmen Abascal, an 87-year-old Spanish woman, the day before her eviction

An 87-year-old Spanish woman was forcibly evicted from the Madrid apartment she had lived in for more than 70 years.

Video showed Maricarmen Abascal, who uses a wheelchair, being taken out of the building in the Spanish capital’s Retiro neighborhood on a stretcher and driven away in an ambulance.

Hundreds of supporters had gathered outside the building to protest her eviction. The case has brought new attention to an ongoing housing crisis in major cities across Spain, as gentrification has caused rents to skyrocket and the stock of affordable housing to shrink.

World.title: Taylor Swift surpasses Beyoncé to become most decorated solo artist in MTV VMAs history
World.content:
Taylor Swift surpassed Beyoncé to become the most-awarded artist in MTV Video Music Awards history on Sunday when she brought her Moon Person statue total to 32.

Swift and Beyoncé were previously tied with 30 VMAs.

Swift won the coveted video of the year award for “The Fate of Ophelia,” dedicating the award to the late Dolly Parton who she described as “the ultimate showgirl.”

“Every single song that she wrote, her storytelling was so vivid and so rich,” Swift said onstage. “Listening to her songs, it’s like watching the best music video you have ever seen in your life every single time you hear what she has written.”

The pop superstar also received the show’s inaugural Artist Director Honors prize, which organizers said was designed to honor someone “whose work behind the camera has expanded the possibilities of music video and advanced the art of visual storytelling.”

Actor Dakota Johnson, a longtime friend of Swift’s, presented the artist with the award, describing her as “an architect of emotional landscapes filled with the most intimate and intricate detail.”

Onstage, Swift reflected on the roughly 60 music videos she has made over the last 20 years, 18 of which she has written and directed.

“I got to tell you, though, the main reason why I love writing and directing music videos so much is because you, the fans, make it so much fun,” Swift said, after thanking MTV and her fans.

The honor comes days after Swift released four new bonus tracks for The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore, a deluxe edition of her 2025 album, The Life of a Showgirl.

After her acceptance speech on Sunday, Swift introduced the premiere of the music video for “Patient Zero,” one of the new tracks on the Encore.

The video, directed by Swift, co-stars Johnson and Oscar-nominee Colin Farrell. Oscar-winner Emmanuel Lubezki, known for “The Revenant” and “Birdman,” did the cinematography.

“With the Patient Zero video, I got to explore the cinematic and literary genres I love so much. I wanted to incorporate elements of gothic ghost stories, true crime, psychological thrillers all in a setting I hadn’t really shot in much,” Swift wrote in a social media post after the video’s debut. “The house was a metaphor for the coldness of a relationship that’s faded and atrophied.”

Following its midnight release on Friday, “Patient Zero” broke the record for the most-streamed song by a female artist in a day so far this year.

The song and the accompanying Encore drop also gave Swift the most streams out of any female artist in a day in 2026.

Other tracks on the album include: “Cleveland!,” “Pink Clouding” and “Babylon.”

World.title: Europe frets as the Kremlin pushes the limits of its hybrid warfare
World.content:
The Kremlin is testing Europe‘s limits.

After months of covert attacks and sabotage across the continent, leaders are warning that Moscow may be about to grow bolder as it seeks to sow chaos and intimidate allies of Ukraine.

Russian President Vladimir Putin could try to test NATO’s resolve to defend members on its eastern flank or respond to attacks that fall short of all-out war, these officials say, at a time when the U.S. is distracted by other conflicts and weighing reducing its military presence in Europe.

An assessment by the Danish Defence Intelligence Service released Thursday warned that in the coming months Moscow will further intensify its campaign of so-called hybrid warfare, “with greater consequences for the targeted countries than in the past.” It also assessed “a low but growing risk that Russia will launch a limited military attack against one or several NATO countries bordering Russia.”

While Moscow has for years embraced tactics that straddle the threshold of war, a string of increasingly brazen incidents in recent months has alarmed U.S. allies.

‘A bit freaked out’

A key moment was the discovery of a Russian drone carrying explosives at an airport in eastern Germany near a Ukrainian aircraft last month. Berlin formally blamed Russia for what it said was a thwarted attack and imposed a diplomatic freeze, though Moscow denied involvement.

That incident appears to have changed the mindset about Russia’s growing threat in Europe, said Ed Arnold, a senior associate fellow in international security at the Royal United Services Institute, a London-based think tank. “It just showed that Putin’s risk calculations are getting more liberal,” Arnold said. “Everyone just got a bit freaked out by that, quite frankly.”

It was followed by the unexpected visit of CIA Director John Ratcliffe to Moscow, during which NATO was discussed.

Incidents have continued to pile up — at defense facilities in Estonia, rail networks in Poland and the power grid in Germany. Many have passed without clear attribution, only intensifying speculation.

All this against the backdrop of near-daily drone incursions into European airspace, fueling anxiety in eastern border towns.

World.title: Inside NBC News’ polling averages: Democrats enjoy biggest lead yet in the race for Congress
World.content:
Democrats are heading into the final stretch of the 2026 midterms with their largest lead yet in the race for Congress and President Donald Trump’s approval rating at a significant low, according to NBC News’ newly released polling averages.

A 9-percentage-point advantage for Democrats when it comes to control of Congress is part of a steady deterioration of the political environment for Republicans. The parties started the road to this November effectively tied in the weeks after President Donald Trump returned to office last year, but independents have gradually begun to prefer a Democratic-controlled Congress. And those voters have soured on Trump and his economic policies in particular.

The congressional average, which stands at 52% to 43% after adjusting to a likely voter scale, measures whether Americans prefer a Congress controlled by Democrats or Republicans before things like individual races and candidates come into play.

Individual polls can bounce around, but an average gives a broad sense of where surveys are trending, and it controls for outliers, which is one reason NBC News released our averages now. At a time when a flurry of polling is released, such as in the homestretch of an election cycle, averages can be valuable tools for tracking what’s happening in the election and diving deeper into how Republicans, Democrats and independents view Trump and the battle for Congress.

The NBC News averages are weighted calculations of all publicly available polls that meet certain standards for methodology and transparency tracking back to the beginning of the second Trump administration.

How NBC News' poll averages work What's the purpose of the polling averages? Our polling averages are designed to measure changes in public opinion over time, rather than reflecting the result of any single survey. They combine national polls using a statistical weighting method that gives greater influence to the polls that are most informative while reducing the effect of random variation from individual surveys. How are these averages put together? Every polling average makes methodological choices about which polls to include and how much influence each should have. This methodology is used for both the NBC News presidential approval average and the generic congressional ballot average. While the underlying calculations differ slightly to reflect the characteristics of each type of polling, the overall approach is the same. Our approach emphasizes five principles: Recency: Newer polls matter more than older polls.

Newer polls matter more than older polls. Precision: Polls with a lower margin of error are weighted higher. The margin of error can be influenced by the number of people in the poll and the amount of weighting needed to make the poll representative.

Polls with a lower margin of error are weighted higher. The margin of error can be influenced by the number of people in the poll and the amount of weighting needed to make the poll representative. Stability: Individual outliers and day-to-day fluctuations have limited influence until they are supported by additional evidence.

Individual outliers and day-to-day fluctuations have limited influence until they are supported by additional evidence. Variety : Frequent pollsters have their older polls downweighted more sharply so that no one firm can dominate the average.

: Frequent pollsters have their older polls downweighted more sharply so that no one firm can dominate the average. Consistency: Polls measuring different populations are placed on the same registered voter scale before being combined. Averages are not predictions. Instead, they aim to provide the clearest possible aggregate measure of the current available polling. Which polls are included? Polls of all adults, registered voters and likely voters are all eligible for inclusion, as are polls with a partisan affiliation provided those surveys meet certain methodological transparency requirements. Polls with partisan affiliations are noted as such whenever possible. NBC News collected all the surveys included in the average. To be eligible for inclusion in the average, a polling organization must, at minimum, meet methodological transparency standards by reporting details on when a poll was conducted and how many respondents were interviewed. If a poll does not publicly release information on field dates, sample size and/or margin of error, it is not included. Why do some polls count more than others? Not every poll contributes equally to the average. Older polls gradually receive less weight as new surveys are released. Likewise, polls with smaller sample sizes or larger margins of error contribute less than more precise surveys. How can I find out more? Check out the full methodology page for the NBC News poll averages here.

With a month to go before the midterm elections, Trump’s approval rating has slid to 39% in the NBC News polling average, with 59% disapproving of his job performance so far. He began his term at 50% approval, according to the average.

Independents drive the shift toward Democrats

There has been little change over time among partisans in the race for Congress, with the vast majorities of Republicans and Democrats standing with their parties consistently.

As a result, much of the shift toward a preference for a Democratic-controlled Congress can be explained by the changing preferences of political independents.

Independents preferred Democrats by about 6 points at the beginning of Trump’s second term, and they slowly moved toward Democrats toward the first half of last year. But things began to shift more rapidly during fall 2025 and early 2026, moving to a lead of about 20 points for Democrats in the spring — as public frustration with Trump’s handling of the economy, the war in Iran and the killings of two Americans by federal immigration officers began to boil over.

The Republican Party hasn’t fully recovered with independents since, and Democrats now hold a 16-point lead among those voters in the race for Congress, according to the average. While survey responses don’t automatically translate into election results, such a strong showing among political independents is one of the many encouraging signs for Democrats heading into the election.

Even so, it’s no guarantee of electoral success for Democrats as Republicans seek to find a way to energize the coalition that sent Trump to the White House just two years ago and narrow the gap before Election Day, more than a month away. Republicans also hope they can defy the political headwinds because so many of the key battleground House and Senate races are being fought in districts and states Trump won in 2024, some by double-digit margins.

What’s behind Trump’s low approval rating

For Trump, movement among independents — and Republicans, to a lesser extent — explains his low marks from voters.

His approval rating among Republicans fluctuated in the mid-to-high 80s for the first six months of his second term, but now, his GOP approval rating is at 79% in a slight but noticeable decline, according to the average.

President Donald Trump speaks in the Oval Office on Sept. 18. Samuel Corum / Bloomberg via Getty Images

Independents’ approval of Trump has dropped further, to 26% in the NBC News average.

Voters have specifically soured on his handling of two of his signature issues — the economy and border security and immigration. In April 2025, an NBC News Decision Desk Poll powered by SurveyMonkey found 40% of American adults approved of Trump’s handling of inflation and the cost of living, while 60% disapproved. By this April’s poll, 32% approved and 68% disapproved.

Inside the averages

Every polling average reflects decisions about which polls to include, how much influence to give them and how to account for differences in whom pollsters survey and how they go about it.

Some polls survey all adults in the U.S., which includes people who aren’t registered to vote or who aren’t eligible to be registered, such as recent immigrants. Other polls specifically survey registered voters.

A third set of polls — which become more frequent as the clock ticks down to Election Day — are polls of a population that pollsters identify as likely voters. Likely voter polls try to capture the attitudes of the group of people who will actually cast ballots, a moving target for polling organizations given the impossible task of predicting voter turnout exactly.

Those three sample universes produce slightly different results on our two key questions. Polls of all adults consistently show a lower approval rating for Trump compared with polls of registered or likely voters. Likely voters are likelier to have made up their mind on the generic ballot question about control of Congress, and as a result, both parties receive higher vote shares among that group.

Both our presidential and congressional averages combine those three universes by adjusting polls of adults and likely voters so they are on the same scale as registered voters. However, because the congressional ballot preference is a question about how people will vote, the congressional average shifts to show a likely voter baseline after Labor Day.

World.title: 2026 MTV VMAs highlights include Madonna, Taylor Swift
World.content:
The 2026 MTV Video Music Awards wowed audiences on Sunday night as Madonna brought out high-energy dance numbers and Taylor Swift made history.

Here are the highlights from the 2026 VMAs.

Madonna performs with Sabrina Carpenter, Charli XCX

Madonna took the VMAs stage at the Peacock Theater in downtown Los Angeles, her first time in over 20 years, announcing: "It's mother."

She opened the show with newly iconic imagery from her recent album, "Confessions II," including green lasers and hordes of cameras following her and Sabrina Carpenter around.

Sabrina Carpenter at The 2026 MTV Video Music Awards. Francis Specker/CBS via Getty Images

The two performed "Bring Your Love" together, which later won the Best Collaboration award, before Madonna transitioned into another dance-fueled club number, "Danceteria" with Charli XCX. The performance featured appearances from others who appeared in "Confessions II — The Film," including Debi Mazar and Julia Garner.

Madonna later took home Artist of the Year.

Charli XCX at The 2026 MTV Video Music Awards. Francis Specker/CBS via Getty Images

Kacey Musgraves pays tribute to Dolly Parton

Kacey Musgraves performs at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards. Matthew Taplinger/CBS via Getty Images

Kacey Musgraves paid tribute to Dolly Parton on Sunday after the VMAs played a short video of the late country music superstar. Musgraves sang "I Will Always Love You," a song Parton released in 1974 that took on a second life when it was later recorded by the late Whitney Houston.

Parton, one of the most groundbreaking and successful musicians in the history of country music, died last month after a brief battle with cancer.

LISA performs "SaWaDiKa"

LISA performs onstage during the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards. Kevin Winter / Getty Images

K-Pop star LISA performed her new single "SaWaDiKa" in the song's TV debut. Part of the performance included the singer riding in the front of Thailand's iconic tuk-tuk taxi.

Earlier in the night, she accepted the Best Pop award for "Dream feat. Kentaro Sakaguchi."

Nirvana accepts Video Vanguard award

Dave Grohl, Krist Novoselic, and Pat Smear of Nirvana accept the Video Vanguard Award onstage during the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards. Kevin Winter / Getty Images

The surviving members of genre-defining grunge band Nirvana were given the Video Vanguard award, recognizing their contribution to the form.

The tribute included archival footage of late frontman Kurt Cobain discussing the process behind the making of several of the band's videos, including "Smells Like Teen Spirit," "Come As You Are" and "Heart-Shaped Box"

Taylor Swift makes VMAs history, debuts "Patient Zero" music video

The VMAs also brought a milestone for Taylor Swift, who was given the VMAs' first-ever Artist Director Honor, which organizers said recognizes artists "whose work behind the camera has expanded the possibilities of music video and advanced the art of visual storytelling."

Swift thanked her fans and everyone she has ever collaborated with on her music videos. She then premiered the music video for her new single "Patient Zero," which stars Dakota Johnson and Colin Farrell.

Taylor Swift accepts the Artist Director Honor onstage during the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards. Kevin Winter / Getty Images

The new accolade made Swift the show's most-awarded artist ever. She was previously tied with Beyoncé, who has 30 Moon Persons.

Swift also won Video of the Year and was nominated in 10 other categories. Swift paid tribute to Parton in her acceptance speech for the final award of the evening.

World.title: Madonna's at the MTV VMAs tonight. Here's what to know about this year's show.
World.content:
The 2026 MTV Video Music Awards are currently airing. See the highlights.

Madonna took the stage as a performer at the MTV Video Music Awards for the first time in over 20 years today as she looks to add to her 20 career wins at the VMAs.

The awards show also brings a milestone for Taylor Swift, who will be given the VMAs' first-ever Artist Director Honors, which organizers said recognizes artists "whose work behind the camera has expanded the possibilities of music video and advanced the art of visual storytelling."

The new accolade guarantees that Swift, who's also nominated in 11 categories, will become the show's most-awarded artist, breaking the tie between her and Beyoncé, who each collected 30 Moon Persons as of 2024. (Neither added to their total in 2025.)

Swift will also be debuting her new "Patient Zero" music video at the VMAs.

Nirvana, meanwhile, will be this year's Video Vanguard Award recipient.

What time do the 2026 VMAs start?

The show starts at 7:30 p.m. ET, 4:30 p.m. PT, on Sunday, Sept. 27.

Who's hosting the 2026 VMAs?

This year's show is being hosted by Snoop Dogg. The rapper known for hits like "Beautiful," "Drop It Like It's Hot" and "Gin and Juice" is no stranger to the VMAs stage, having first performed at the show in 1994 and winning three times during his career.

Snoop Dogg at the 2022 MTV VMAs at the Prudential Center in Newark, New Jersey. Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for MTV/Paramount Global

Where to watch the 2026 VMAs

The VMAs will be airing on CBS television stations (find your local station here) and on MTV. The show will also be streaming on Paramount+.

How to watch the VMAs red carpet

See the stars arrive and check out the best looks from the red carpet in special coverage streaming live on CBS News Los Angeles starting at 6 p.m. ET, 3 p.m. PT, ahead of the VMAs.

Who are the VMA performers this year?

Along with Madonna's highly anticipated return, the performances at this year's VMAs include a special tribute to Dolly Parton by Kacey Musgraves, who is nominated in the best country category.

Here's a list of the announced VMA performers, in alphabetical order:

When Madonna last performed at the VMAs in August 2003, George W. Bush was in the White House, the U.S. was five months into the Iraq War, and Mark Zuckerberg was a few months away from launching what's now known as Facebook.

This year, a performance by the 68-year-old Queen of Pop will open the VMAs. She's up for 13 awards, the most of any nominee of the night. If she sweeps all 13 categories, her career total will go up to 33.

Madonna leads the 2026 nominees for the MTV Video Music Awards and will perform at the VMAs for the first time in over 20 years. Courtesy of Warner Records

LISA, a member of the K-pop group Blackpink and a four-time nominee this year, will be taking the stage to perform her new single "SaWaDiKa." First-time nominees GENER8ION and Swedish rapper Yung Lean, whose song "Storm" is up for four awards, will perform the world premiere of "Storm II."

Singer-songwriter Sombr, nominated in three categories, will join RAYE, whose hit "Where Is My Husband!" is up for song of the year, and Teddy Swims in a tribute performance for George Michael, who died in 2016. The tribute comes nearly 40 years after the release of his first solo album, "Faith."

Country and hip-hop artist Shaboozey will sing "Cowgirl," which received two nominations. He'll also join Gunna for their collaboration "High Noon."

Best new artist nominee Sienna Spiro will also take the stage during the night.

Fan voting in most categories closed Friday, but fans can still cast ballots for best new artist and song of the summer. Voting for the summer's top tune will be happening on MTV's Instagram Stories until 11 a.m. ET Sunday. Fans can vote for best new artist online even after the show starts.
