World.title: Iraq starts receiving gasoline from Syria
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq has officially started importing gasoline through Syria, creating a crucial overland energy corridor between the two nations.

This transit route serves as a critical alternative for Baghdad to secure vital fuel supplies amid difficulties facing maritime shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.

The initial consignment consisted of roughly 32,800 metric tons of high-octane gasoline brought by sea from the United States. The shipment arrived at Syria’s Baniyas port aboard the Marshall Islands-flagged tanker Avanti.

The fuel was moved to storage tanks at the Baniyas refinery before being loaded into tanker trucks. At least 77 tanker trucks have already left the port, headed toward Iraq’s Baiji refinery, according to Reuters.

A transit contract between the state-owned Syrian Petroleum Company (SPC) and Qatar’s UCC Holding, which provided the gasoline and is in charge of logistics, governs the operation.

Iraq’s State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) has finalized the agreement to ensure the continuity of these supplies.

The route was only used in one direction, transporting Iraqi fuel oil by road to the Syrian port of Baniyas before being exported out by sea, reaching the US market for the first time in July.

According to officials, while the present transportation arrangement only covers gasoline, the corridor might potentially grow to include other petroleum products, crude oil, and other items.

World.title: Vitol becomes second-largest buyer of Iraq’s oil after UAE’s ADNOC
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Vitol has strengthened its presence in the Iraqi oil market by purchasing at least 25 million barrels of crude in September 2026, a move reflecting how major oil traders are capitalizing on supply disruptions in the Gulf region.

The Swiss-based Dutch multinational energy and commodity trading company is leveraging its shipping and logistics capabilities to provide export outlets for Iraqi crude amid the challenges facing tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz due to the conflict between the United States and Iran.

These purchases come as Baghdad seeks to maintain oil flows to global markets following a decline in exports during the early months of the war, when securing the transport of shipments from Iraq’s southern ports proved difficult.

The deal highlights the shifting dynamics of the Middle East oil trade, where the ability to secure tankers and arrange transportation has become a critical factor in accessing crude oil, alongside Iraq’s use of price discounts to attract buyers willing to take on shipping risks.

Vitol has purchased between 25 and 30 million barrels of Iraqi crude scheduled for loading this September.

An official in the Iraqi energy sector indicated that the company’s share amounted to approximately 25 million barrels, according to Reuters.

Vitol has become the second-largest buyer of Iraqi oil this month, trailing the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC), which purchased approximately 40 million barrels, compared to about 32 million barrels in August.

The moves came amid a drop in Iraq’s oil exports during the early months of the conflict, owing to the country’s ports’ position in the northern Arabian Gulf and the lack of its own shipping fleet, which hindered petroleum delivery to global markets.

According to data from Kpler, a leading data platform that tracks commodity flows and maritime shipping, Iraqi oil exports from southern ports averaged approximately 2.35 million barrels per day in August.

In August, Iran granted a number of Iraqi oil tankers permission to transit the Strait of Hormuz, following repeated requests from Baghdad for arrangements to ensure continued oil exports.

Iraqi oil shipments face challenges due to navigational risks in the Strait of Hormuz. Vessels transiting the waterway are exposed to the threat of Iranian attacks, prompting buyers to demand price discounts to offset higher transportation and insurance costs.

World.title: Iraq studies proposals to store oil in Oman, Egypt, Singapore
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is studying proposals to store crude oil in storage facilities in countries including Egypt, Oman, and Singapore.

The spokesperson for the Iraqi Oil Ministry, Salim al-Rikabi, told Attaqa News that the government is studying proposals to participate in refinery and storage projects outside Iraq to select the best options.

To move forward with storing crude oil in Egypt, Iraq needs to complete the Basra-Haditha pipeline project, which would then extend out toward the Jordanian port of Aqaba and finally to the city of Arish in the northeastern Sinai Peninsula, according to al-Rikabi.

In September 2025, Iraq’s State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) has signed two agreements with OQ, formerly known as Oman Oil Company, and its subsidiary, Oman Tank Terminal Company (OTTCO).

The first agreement establishes a strategic partnership to develop an integrated project to store Iraqi crude oil in the Special Economic Zone at Duqm (SEZD), the largest special economic zone in the Middle East and North Africa.

The second agreement outlines OQ’s responsibility to market Iraqi crude oil in global markets. The deal aims to leverage the administrative and commercial strengths of both parties to enhance the trading value of Iraqi crude oil internationally.

The proposals are part of the Iraqi government’s effort to bypass the Strait of Hormuz—the main route for the country’s oil exports—where maritime shipping has been facing difficulties since the start of the military conflict involving the United States, Israel, and Iran.

Since the outbreak of the war on February 28 and the subsequent closure of the Strait of Hormuz, Iraq’s seaborne oil exports collapsed to unprecedented levels.

Iraq’s oil exports fell to approximately 550,000 barrels per day in March, 132,000 barrels per day in April, and 98,000 barrels per day in May, before gradually rising to 2.16 million barrels per day in August.

World.title: International coalition halts financial aid to Peshmerga
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The US-led international coalition has officially halted financial aid to Iraqi Kurdistan’s Peshmerga forces following the expiration of a four-year agreement.

The Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) and the United States Department of Defense inked an agreement that extended from September 21, 2022, until September 21, 2026.

On Thursday, the troops received their final allowance for August and September 2026.

According to the Secretary-General of the Ministry of Peshmerga Affairs, Bakhtiar Sadiq, the financial aid under the initial agreement was planned to steadily reduce by 25 percent each year until reaching a complete halt.

This cash halt aligns with the overall conclusion of the international coalition’s military operations in Iraq, with a full stoppage of combat and training responsibilities expected by September 30, 2026.

Additionally, the proposed US Counter-ISIS Train and Equip Fund (CTEF) plan for 2027 includes no support for the Peshmerga.

The international coalition has tied its financial assistance to necessary reforms and the unification of the Peshmerga forces, particularly the integration of politically separated units. Earlier in September, the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) publicly announced that the unification process was complete.

To address the newly established funding imbalance, the Ministry of Peshmerga Affairs has formally requested the federal government in Baghdad to adjust Peshmerga salaries to align them permanently with federal Iraqi military and security forces.

World.title: Iraq seeks US exemption to resume Iranian flights
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi government revealed on Saturday that it is holding discussions with the US administration to obtain an exemption for certain Iraqi airports from the ban on Iranian airline flights imposed under US sanctions, citing the disruption caused to traveling patients, students, and pilgrims.

According to the Iraqi Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), the Iraqi government is engaged in direct talks with the US side to exempt specific Iraqi airports from these measures.

The exception would allow for the resumption of flights for humanitarian grounds, which include medical care, education, religious pilgrimages, and civilian interests.

Iranian airlines primarily handle the transport of Iranians traveling to Iraq in large numbers to visit the shrines of Shiite Imams, as well as Iraqis flying to Iran for religious pilgrimages, studies, or medical treatment.

Iraq joined several other nations in suspending Iranian flights to and from its territory after US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that all Iranian airlines will cease operations as of September 23.

Under the new measures, any country or firm that provides services to Iranian aircraft is completely removed from the global US dollar system. The services include fueling airplanes, offering ground handling and landing services, and selling passenger tickets.

World.title: Iraq unveils plan for data centers in Baghdad, Basra, and Mosul
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Communications unveiled an ambitious strategic blueprint on Saturday, September 26, 2026, to construct a distributed network of enterprise data centers across Baghdad, Basra, and Mosul, aiming to upgrade national digital infrastructure and localize hosting for global technology conglomerates.

In an exclusive statement granted to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), the Director General of the General Company for Communications and Informatics, Ali Yassin, confirmed that establishing tier-standard data centers across multiple provinces stands among the ministry’s top executive priorities to accelerate digital transformation.

Yassin revealed that the capital city of Baghdad will host three dedicated data centers situated across prime connectivity hubs, specifically at the Al-Sinak telecommunications complex, the Al-Intisar facility, and the Al-Mamoun Telecommunications Tower compound adjacent to the ministry’s headquarters.

The geographical distribution within the capital ensures redundant network routing, continuous uptime, and high-speed fiber interconnection to support both federal e-governance platforms and commercial cloud services.

Beyond Baghdad, the national strategy targets key regional logistics and transit corridors, including a specialized facility planned in Basra Governorate in close proximity to the international submarine cable landing station, directly capitalizing on Iraq’s high-capacity maritime fiber-optic gateways.

Additionally, the ministry is preparing to establish another facility in Mosul to anchor cloud architecture across the northern provinces.

Yassin emphasized that these specialized data centers are purpose-built to attract major multinational technology companies, creating localized environments capable of hosting global content, accelerating low-latency data delivery, and reinforcing Iraq’s sovereign digital ecosystem.

World.title: Iraq reaches 100,000 LPG converted cars as Parliament urges factory model access
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Gas Filling and Services Company, an operating affiliate of the Iraqi Ministry of Oil, announced on Saturday, September 26, 2026, that the cumulative number of vehicles converted to run on liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) has reached approximately 100,000 across Iraq.

Speaking to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), the company’s media director, Mahdi Al-Nouri, confirmed that retrofitted vehicle figures currently range between 98,000 and 100,000 cars, noting an escalating pace of adoption among motorists seeking economical alternatives to conventional liquid fuels.

Al-Nouri stated that installation and technical maintenance services are carried out across a nationwide network of 26 specialized workshops operating under the state-owned gas company.

The growing consumer uptake reflects heightened public interest in cleaner, subsidized autogas, prompting the Ministry of Oil to scale up workshop throughput and expand fueling station capacity to keep up with escalating demand.

Despite this milestone, converted vehicles represent a modest fraction—less than 1.5 percent—of Iraq’s national automobile fleet, which currently totals approximately 7 million registered cars. The autogas initiative has simultaneously sparked parliamentary scrutiny regarding regulatory bottlenecks.

Lawmaker Amer Abdul-Jabbar raised the issue on the floor of the Council of Representatives, criticizing the Ministry of Oil for restricting autogas dispensing exclusively to locally converted vehicles while denying fuel to imported cars equipped with factory-installed LPG systems.

Abdul-Jabbar called on the federal government to reform existing fuel distribution policies, authorize gas sales for all compatible vehicles, and incentivize the commercial importation of factory-built LPG cars to accelerate emissions reduction and alleviate domestic gasoline consumption.

World.title: Iraq launches first smart pneumatic waste collection system with Spanish backing
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s National Investment Commission (NIC), in coordination with the Ministry of Environment and the Spanish Embassy in Baghdad, officially launched the country’s first smart automated pneumatic waste collection system (URD) on Saturday, September 26, 2026, marking a pivotal milestone in the modernization of municipal sanitation and sustainable urban management.

The initiative introduces advanced underground vacuum collection networks designed to eliminate conventional curbside dumpsters and heavy collection vehicular traffic across newly planned smart cities and licensed residential investment developments.

Speaking at the launch conference attended by an Iraqi News Agency (INA) correspondent, NIC Deputy Chairman Salar Mohammed Amin affirmed that the adoption of the URD pneumatic network represents a comprehensive national initiative requiring deep cross-institutional synergy between public ministries, municipal directorates, and private developers.

He revealed that the commission has already secured all statutory and regulatory approvals to mandate the underground system within master plans for new satellite cities and residential complexes, establishing a national technical committee alongside the Ministry of Environment to oversee phased execution and enforce strict environmental compliance benchmarks.

Amin emphasized that sustainable investment must transcend structural brick-and-mortar construction to create integrated, livable urban ecosystems that elevate daily public health and quality of life.

He noted that operational success relies on an interconnected institutional network encompassing the Ministry of Construction, Housing, Municipalities and Public Works, the Municipality of Baghdad, local governorate authorities, the Ministry of Electricity, and telecommunications operators, working collectively to provide dedicated power grids, subterranean civil infrastructure, and smart sensor integration necessary for automated municipal services.

Spanish Ambassador to Iraq Alicia Rico Pérez del Pulgar underscored that the rollout of the pneumatic vacuum infrastructure represents a substantial qualitative leap toward modernizing waste management practices through cleaner, more energy-efficient technologies.

Highlighting Madrid’s dedication to technical knowledge transfer and bilateral capacity building, the ambassador framed the project as a catalyst for expanded Spanish-Iraqi commercial and environmental partnerships in green infrastructure, renewable energy, and smart city urban planning, calling upon public institutions and private enterprises from both nations to leverage the project into enduring bilateral economic cooperation.

World.title: India to join SCO national coordinators meeting in Islamabad
World.content:
Pakistan to host SCO coordinatorsâ meet from Sept 28-30

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

India will participate in a meeting of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) national coordinators that Pakistan will host on September 28-30, official sources said. The meeting is expected to approve the calendar of events under Pakistanâs presidency, leading up to the Council of Heads of State (CHS) summit for which Islamabad will soon send out invitations to the leaders of all member-states of the Eurasian bloc, including PM Narendra Modi.After joining the China-dominated grouping in 2017 as a full member, India has participated actively in various SCO mechanisms, with Modi representing India at the heads of state summits and external affairs minister S Jaishankar joining the heads of government meetings.Unlike with SAARC, India has ringfenced its involvement in SCO from outstanding bilateral differences with Pakistan, mainly the core issue of cross-border terrorism, while consistently reminding the Organisation that one of its original mandates was to fight terrorism, extremism and separatism. Government has backed SCO connectivity initiatives too but with the rider that these must respect sovereignty and territorial integrity of all States.Indiaâs national coordinator Alok Dimri is expected to participate in the national coordinatorsâ meeting that will begin on Monday. Even without any substantive bilateral engagement for a decade, India and Pakistan have regularly seen their officials visiting each otherâs country for SCO-related exercises and Jaishankar himself travelled to Pakistan in 2024 for the SCO heads of government meeting.However, the key question remains â even if itâs too early to ask â whether Modi will attend the summit in Islamabad next year. The SAARC summit process remains blocked because of the PMâs reluctance to travel to Pakistan and, barring a dramatic change in the situation, the PM is unlikely to visit Islamabad.According to Indian officials, any such change can only be effected by Islamabad through tangible and irreversible action against cross-border terrorism and UN-proscribed terror entities operating out of Pakistan. Government recently denied strongly that it is involved even in any track 2 dialogue with Islamabad.Pakistan had assumed presidency of the SCO at the Bishkek summit earlier this month. Modi said the same day in his address that countries that use terrorism as an instrument of state policy, providing shelter to terrorists, must be categorically told terrorism can never be a strategic asset for anyone.

World.title: Despite rainfall deficit, kharif acreage above 5-year average
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Overall acreage of kharif (summer-sown) crops in the country declined by just over 1% this year compared with last year and while the dip was expected due to deficient monsoon rainfall this year, the sowing season still ended up recording higher than 'normal' (average of last five years) acreage.

Though only marginally above the 'normal', it reflects tweaks in farmers' strategy if warning comes in advance.

Latest acreage data shows total sown area at 1,107 lakh hectares (ha) as of Friday was 3 lakh ha more than 'normal' acreage (1,104 lakh ha) despite a cumulative deficit of 12% (June 1-Sept 26) in monsoon rainfall. In the same period in 2025, which recorded 8% more than normal (surplus) rainfall, total acreage was 1,121 lakh ha.

The most popular kharif crop and one of the most water-intensive, paddy, reported a 3.6% decline in acreage compared with last year, but this was still 4.6% higher than the 'normal' acreage. Another guzzler, sugarcane, too reported higher acreage than its normal sown area, reflecting farmers' preference for crops which assure them of better returns, even as they had to depend on excessive use of groundwater, at the risk of high input cost.





The real test of what rainfall deficit will entail, however, may be reflected in the yield of these crops, first estimates for which will soon be released by the Union agriculture ministry. The output of pulses (mainly pigeon peas), oilseeds (mainly soybean and groundnut), cotton and coarse cereals (mainly bajra and maize) may be a real concern due to deficient and skewed distribution of rainfall in the 'monsoon core zone' - the large part of central India and Bihar which depend on seasonal rains for farming in absence of adequate irrigation coverage.

Floods in certain parts of Bihar and Assam, and drought in parts of Maharashtra and Karnataka may also negatively impact the overall output.

Apprehending the impact of deficient monsoon rainfall on the rabi (winter-sown) crops due to low moisture content in the soil and shortage of water for irrigation, the agriculture ministry will discuss contingency measures at a two-day meet starting Monday.

World.title: 'Use lowest effective dose of Nsaids': Fresh advisory on kidney risks of painkiller abuse
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) has issued a fresh advisory on rational consumption of painkillers and antibiotics, in view of their repeated use, without proper medical advice, putting people at the risk of kidney complications and other adverse effects.

The drug regulator's circular says non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (Nsaids) and antibiotics are prescription medicines under Drugs and Cosmetics Rules and should be used only when clinically indicated, at the appropriate dose and duration and under medical supervision. It has asked people not to take Nsaids, commonly used as painkillers, repeatedly or for a prolonged period without advice.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation has also cautioned against self-medication with antibiotics and advised people with existing kidney disease or other risk factors for renal impairment to inform their doctor before taking Nsaids.

Prof Sandeep Mahajan, nephrologist at AIIMS, said unregulated and prolonged use of painkillers can accelerate the decline in kidney function. "All prescription medicines should be taken under the supervision of a qualified physician, with the prescribed dose and duration strictly followed."

CDSCO has advised doctors to use the lowest effective dose of Nsaids for the shortest appropriate duration, with extra caution in patients at risk of kidney injury. This comes against the backdrop of a substantial chronic kidney disease burden in India. A 2025 review of community-based studies estimated pooled chronic kidney disease prevalence at 13.24%, although estimates varied widely across regions and studies.

World.title: Balakot to Sindoor, India gave befitting reply: PM Modi on Pakistan terror
World.content:
PM Modiâs stern message to Pakistan: âTime for sponsoring terror to go unpunished is long goneâ

'Zero-tolerance terror policy has borne results'

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a stern message to Pakistan, PM Modi said on Sunday the time when its role in sponsoring terror attacks on India would go unpunished is long gone, and his govt has made it clear with its actions, including Op Sindoor, that terrorists will be given a befitting response for their sinister designs against India.Modi's message came in his 'Mann ki Baat' broadcast as India marks the 10th anniversary of the surgical strikes on terror hideouts in Pakistan on Sept 28-29, 2016. "The world was astonished to see the manner in which our brave soldiers crossed the LoC to take action against terror. The strike demonstrated a new aspect of India's counter-terror policy. It was our decisive response to long-standing pain India had endured," he said."Over the past decade, from Balakot airstrike to Op Sindoor, India has repeatedly sent out a clear message: if terrorists dare to cast an evil eye on India, they will be met with a befitting response."Contrasting his government's targeted action against Pakistan to the approach of the previous Congress-led UPA govt, PM Narendra Modi said serial blasts had once become a common occurrence in the country. On Sept 13, 2008, serial blasts rocked Delhi and, just a few weeks later, the Mumbai terror attack stunned the country, the PM said.Demands for action against Pakistan following every terror attack used to be made then but were ignored. "Today, India pursues a zero-tolerance policy against terrorism, and we are witnessing the results of that," he said.During Op Sindoor, the Modi govt also unveiled a tougher national security doctrine, declaring that any future terror attack will be treated as an act of war. This eliminated the false distinction between terrorists and their state sponsors, it had said.Modi's message to Pakistan comes at a time when the nation is trying to airbrush its long association with terror incidents around the world, reflected in its PM Shehbaz Sharif's recent claims at the United Nations General Assembly about its role and sacrifices in combating terrorism.In his UNGA address, foreign minister S Jaishankar had snubbed Pakistan, calling it a "serial practitioner of terrorism" and asserting that India will continue to exercise its right to defend itself against terror threats.

World.title: LPU protests: Over 2,000 police deployed after stone-pelting, vehicles set ablaze
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Punjab Police deployed more than 2,000 personnel at Lovely Professional University (LPU) after student protests over an alleged rape case turned violent on Sunday, with senior officers saying the situation had been brought under control.

ADGP M F Farooqui told news agency ANI, that the force would remain deployed on campus through the night to maintain security.

âWe will ensure security on the campus throughout the night... A force of over 2,000 personnel is currently deployed here. Law and order has been fully maintained and restored... The process is ongoing, and we are working to keep the situation under control,â Farooqui told ANI.

He appealed to families not to panic, saying, âTo the families whose daughters are staying in the hostel here: please do not worry; everyone is safe...

The atmosphere here is completely calm, and the university students are also cooperating with us in restoring peace...â

Fresh violence erupted on Sunday evening after the protesting students pelted stones at police personnel and attacked their vehicles, leaving several cops injured, officials said.

The protests began after claims circulated on social media about the alleged rape of a university student on the LPU campus.





Students later blocked National Highway 44 outside the university from around 8 am, according to officials.

Police said the situation escalated when protesters allegedly pelted stones at personnel and attacked police vehicles. Officers used a lathi charge as they attempted to clear the highway, after which protesters moved towards the campus.

Two police vehicles were set on fire, while several police personnel were injured.

Jalandhar Police Commissioner Satinder Singh said reports of disturbances inside hostels were rumours and that checks had found no such incidents.

âFirst of all, reports of disturbances in the hostels were merely rumours. All hostels have been checked, and there are no issues. Traffic has resumed, and the situation is normal,â Singh said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

He added, âOther matters will be resolved through discussions with the students...

Overall, the atmosphere is fine, and any minor issues will be addressed... Please inform the families that all students are safe and there is no cause for concern.â

DIG (Jalandhar Range) Naveen Singla also said, âThe situation has been brought under control. Traffic movement on NH-44 will be restored soon.â

Meanwhile, LPU postponed its mid-term examinations until further notice and suspended regular classes for 10 days from September 28. The university urged students to remain calm, follow official instructions and stay connected for further updates.

Police said the deployment would continue overnight as authorities work to maintain order on campus and assess the situation.

World.title: HM Amit Shah recalls Ashok Singhal's role in Ram temple movement
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Lauding former VHP leader Ashok Singhal as an inspiration and hero, home minister

World.title: Boeing flags 737 MAX glitch that may turn off auto pilot
World.content:
A software issue could disengage the B737 MAX autopilot during certain go-arounds when pilots alter the aircraftâs planned altitude or flight path.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Boeing has identified a software issue that could potentially lead to auto pilot disengaging during certain go-arounds (aborting landing to take off again and make a second attempt) on the B737 MAX when pilots change their planned altitude and path. India has about 100 of these aircraft between Air India Express and Akasa.Aviation insiders say this is not a safety scare and Boeing has issued an advisory to pilots regarding what to do in the rare event of a B737 MAX going around and then the altitude window being changed from what is in the system for that particular sector.A Boeing spokesperson said: "Last month, we informed all 737 operators about a software issue where pilots may not have access to automated flight guidance during a specific landing scenario. We shared information with operators that reinforced existing pilot procedures for safely handling such cases. Our engineers are working on a software update to permanently address the issue."A spokesperson for Akasa said: "We are closely coordinating with Boeing and can confirm there is no impact to safety... Our aircraft continue to operate safely in accordance with established procedures and applicable regulatory requirements."AI Express has over 50 of these planes.US Federal Aviation Admi-nistration has said in a statem-ent that it will "convene a corrective action review board and take immediate action if it identifies a safety concern".What was to be Boeing's answer to rival Airbus's best-selling A320 new engine option which boasts lower fuel burns, the B737 MAX came under intense scrutiny soon after it entered commercial passenger service in May 2017. Two back-to-back MAX crashes within five months - Lion Air in Oct 2018 and Ethiopian Airlines in March 2019 - that left 346 people dead led to the aircraft being grounded globally in March 2019. After Boeing made some crucial changes, the aircraft was allowed to fly again in Dec 2020.

World.title: Post-Ganeshotsav clean-up in Mumbai: 934 tonnes of offerings collected, 34 tonnes of waste cleared from Juhu beach
World.content:
The BMC has collected around 934 metric tonnes of nirmalya during this year’s Ganeshotsav, while a post-immersion clean-up at Juhu beach on Saturday (September 26, 2026) cleared another 34 tonnes of waste.

The civic body’s Solid Waste Management Department had deployed 613 nirmalya (religious offerings) collection containers and 838 vehicles at immersion sites across Mumbai to separately collect floral and other religious offerings generated during the festival.

Following the final Ganesh idol immersions on Anant Chaturdashi on Friday (September 25, 2026), the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) also undertook an extensive clean-up operation along immersion routes, roads and other public spaces across the city.

Around 10,000 additional sanitation workers, along with cleaning machinery, were deployed for the operation, according to the civic body.

At Juhu beach, around 34 tonnes of waste were collected early on Saturday (September 26, 2026) as part of the ‘Sea, Shore, Shine-2026’ clean-up campaign, organised jointly by the Divyaj Foundation, BMC, Mumbai Police and MeghaShrey. School students, volunteers, representatives of NGOs and citizens participated in the drive.

The Juhu operation was among the clean-up efforts undertaken following the conclusion of Ganeshotsav, during which large crowds and immersion processions converge on Mumbai’s beaches and other immersion sites.

The BMC is also separately processing nirmalya collected after the immersions instead of disposing of all the material as waste.

At Juhu beach, the civic body and Dr Nanasaheb Dharmadhikari Pratishthan are segregating flowers from the collected nirmalya. The flowers will be processed to produce incense sticks and other usable products, the civic body said. Municipal Commissioner Ashwini Bhide visited the collection and processing operation on Saturday (Septembmer 26, 2026).

Ms. Bhide said Mumbai’s sea and coastline are important natural assets and urged citizens to avoid dumping plastic and other waste on beaches and in public places, even after the festival.

The post-immersion measures are also supported by the BMC’s ‘One Ganpati, One Tree’ initiative, under which the civic body plans to plant as many trees as Ganesh idols are immersed in Mumbai this year. The initiative is aimed at linking Ganeshotsav with longer-term tree plantation and conservation efforts.

As part of the initiative, Mayor Ritu Tawde planted tulsi and sunflower saplings at the Mayor’s residence in Byculla on Saturday (September 25, 2026) using clay and water left after immersing a shadu-clay Ganesh idol. She appealed to residents, housing societies, and Ganesh mandals to similarly reuse clay from eco-friendly idols for planting and nurturing saplings.

Meanwhile, the Juhu clean-up was attended by Divyaj Foundation founder Amruta Fadnavis, actor Ajay Devgn, State Minister Mangal Prabhat Lodha, MLAs Amit Satam and Ram Kadam, BMC Commissioner Ashwini Bhide and other civic officials and volunteers.

Ms. Fadnavis said maintaining cleanliness after festivals required collective participation, while Devgn urged citizens to treat keeping their city clean with the same responsibility with which they maintain their homes.

World.title: Asian Games 2026 India’s medallists: Full list of winners
World.content:
The 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games are underway in Japan. India is currently placed at the 12th spot on the medals’ table with 37 medals. China is leading the table with 208 medals. Japan is second with 157 medals and Republic of Korea is third with 84 medals.

On Sunday (September 27, 2026), India’s Abhay Singh settled for an Asian Games silver medal after going down against Eain Yow Ng of Malaysia in the men’s singles final of the squash competition, and junior world champion Anahat Singh similarly secured a hard-fought Silver in the women’s singles final against Malaysia’s Sivasangari Subramaniam.

Harita Bhadra clinched bronze in the women’s 200m at the Asian Games. Long jumper Ancy Sojan secured silver in the women’s long jump, while Sarvesh Kushare claimed silver in the men’s high jump.

Tejaswin Shankar, meanwhile, secured his second Asian Games medal, winning bronze in the decathlon following the two-day competition.

Parul Chaudhary bettered her personal best on her way to bronze in the women’s 3000m steeplechase at the Asian Games.

On Saturday (September 26), India’s Sawan Barwal won a silver medal in the men’s marathon. India’s women’s kabaddi team extended their dominance at the Asian Games securing yet another gold medal after a thrilling 37-34 win over Iran in the finals. The men’s hockey team continued it’s winning streak, defeating Japan by 2-0, securing the semifinal berth in the big-ticket sports event.

Simultaneously, the squash squad led by teen-sensation Anahat Singh and Abhay Shetty in singles category stormed into the final game. The duo will be competing for a gold medal in their final game on Sunday.

Women’s 50m rifle 3P team comprising of Vidarsa Vinod, Ashi Chouksey, Tilottama Sen won the silver medal. Mixed squash doubles team including Joshana Chinappa, Velavan Senthilkumar clinched the bronze medal.

On Friday (September 25), the duo of Manush Shah and Diya Chitale secured a historic bronze medal in table tennis mixed doubles after stunning the world No. 4 pair from Hong Kong to enter the semi-finals.

Baranica Elangovan entered her name in the record books by winning a historic bronze medal for India in the women’s pole vault event at the Asian Games

Indian long-distance runner Gulveer Singh upgraded his Asian Games medal from bronze to silver in the men’s 10,000m.

India’s Manpreet Kaur clinched the bronze medal in women’s shot put competition of the Asian Games with an effort of 17.17m in Nagoya on Friday (September 25).

Kamaljeet and Suruchi Singh won gold in the mixed team 10m air pistol event. The Indian team, comprising Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar, Rudranksh Patil and Niraj Kumar, won silver in the men’s 50m rifle 3P team event.

The Indian 4x400m mixed relay quartet of Vishal T.K., M.R. Poovamma, Manu T.S. and Vithya Ramraj earned a silver medal in the final at the Paloma Mizuho Stadium.

Manpreet Kaur clinched a bronze medal in the Women’s Shot Put final with a season-best throw of 17.17 meters.

The duo of Manush Shah and Diya Chitale secured a historic bronze in Table Tennis Mixed Doubles after stunning the world No. 4 pair from Hong Kong to enter the semi-finals.

Seema Kumari, competing in her first Asiad, won a bronze medal in the 10,000m at the Asian Games, 16 years after Preeja Sreedharan and Kavita Raut’s historic gold-silver double in 2010.

Manipur’s Naorem Roshibina Devi won her third consecutive Asian Games medal, clinching silver after losing to Zhang Xiaoyu in the women’s 60kg wushu final on Thursday (September 24, 2026).

Jay Meena secured India’s first-ever soft tennis medal at the Asian Games, fetching a bronze after losing to Japan’s Takuya Kurosaka in the men’s singles semifinals. Star Indian weightlifter Mirabai Chanu completed her medal collection, winning a silver medal in the women’s 49kg event in the Asian Games.

Lakshya Sen and Ayush Shetty faltered against higher-ranked opponents as the Indian men’s team concluded with a bronze medal after losing 1-3 to their rivals, China, in the semifinals.

The Indian Women’s Cricket Team clinched a historic victory at the Karogi Athletic Park in Nisshin, Aichi. Facing off against Sri Lanka in a high-stakes final, the Women in Blue triumphed to secure India’s very first gold medal of the tournament.

Meanwhile, shooters have led the charge for India. The women’s skeet team, comprising Raiza Dhillon, Maheshwari Chauhan and Parinaaz Dhaliwal, won a bronze with a combined score of 331 here on September 23, 2026.

Experienced rifle shooter Elavenil Valarivan played a starring role in the country’s double-silver haul in the women’s 10m air rifle competition. Elavenil, one of India’s most accomplished rifle shooters, helped the country secure silver in the team event along with Sonam Maskar and Vidarsa Vinod. She then went on to add an individual silver.

For the men’s side, teenager Himanshu Dhillon produced a superb performance to win silver, while former world champion Rudrankksh Patil clinched bronze as India secured two individual podium finishes in the men’s 10m air rifle event. The two then teamed up with Parth Mane to win another silver in the team event, finishing just behind China.

After an impressive start in shooting, India also managed to script history in Mixed Martial Arts (MMA), with Suchika Tariyal winning the nation’s first-ever bronze medal for MMA at the Asian Games.

A contingent of 501 Indian athletes, comprising 267 men and 234 women, is competing across 36 disciplines in the 2026 edition. Apart from shooting, athletics and archery too are expected to add to the medal tally. India is also defending both the men’s and women’s titles in cricket and kabaddi.

World.title: Asian Games 2026 Medal Tally: Anahat, Abhay, Sarvesh win silver medals, Parul Chaudhary sets new record
World.content:
At the Asian Games 2026, India’s India’s Harita Bhadra clinched bronze in the women’s 200m at the Asian Games. Long jumper Ancy Sojan secured silver in the women’s long jump, while Sarvesh Kushare claimed silver in the men’s high jump.

Tejaswin Shankar, meanwhile, secured his second Asian Games medal, winning bronze in the decathlon following the two-day competition.

Parul Chaudhary bettered her personal best on her way to bronze in the women’s 3000m steeplechase at the Asian Games.

Abhay Singh settled for a silver medal after going down against Eain Yow Ng of Malaysia in the men’s singles final of the squash competition, and junior world champion Anahat Singh similarly secured a hard-fought silver in the women’s singles final against Malaysia’s Sivasangari Subramaniam.

India won a silver medal at the men’s marathon event with Sawan Barwal shattering his own national record and ending a 41-year-old medal drought for in the sport for the country. Tajinder Pal Singh Toor also won a silver in shot put. Prachi Choudhary also won a bronze medal in the Women’s 400 m event at the Asian Games.

Also Read: Asian Games 2026 India’s medallists: Full list of winners

On Saturday (September 26, 2026), India’s women’s kabaddi team extended their dominance at the Asian Games securing yet another gold medal after a thrilling 37-34 win over Iran in the finals.

Meanwhile, India’s Sawan Barwal won a silver medal in the men’s marathon. Women’s 50m rifle 3P team comprising of Vidarsa Vinod, Ashi Chouksey, Tilottama Sen won the silver medal. Mixed squash doubles team including Joshana Chinappa, Velavan Senthilkumar clinched the bronze medal.

On Friday (September 25, 2026), the duo of Manush Shah and Diya Chitale secured a historic bronze medal in table tennis mixed doubles after stunning the world No. 4 pair from Hong Kong to enter the semi-finals.

Baranica Elangovan entered the record books by winning a historic bronze medal for India in the women’s pole vault event at the Asian Games.

Indian long-distance runner Gulveer Singh upgraded his Asian Games medal from bronze to silver in the men’s 10,000m.

India’s Manpreet Kaur clinched the bronze medal in the women’s shot put competition at the Asian Games with an effort of 17.17m in Nagoya on Friday (September 25, 2026).

In another major development at the Games, India’s Kamaljeet and Suruchi Singh clinched the gold medal in the mixed team 10m air pistol event.

The Indian team, comprising Aishwary Pratap Singh Tomar, Rudranksh Patil and Niraj Kumar, won silver in the men’s 50m rifle 3P team event.

Indian 4x400m mixed relay team win a silver medal in the final event at the Paloma Mizuho stadium.

Manpreet Kaur clinched a bronze medal in the Women’s Shot Put final with a season-best throw of 17.17 meters.

Seema Kumari, meanwhile, became only the third Indian woman to medal in the 10,000m at the Asian Games, after Preeja Sreedharan and Kavita Raut’s historic gold-silver double back in 2010.

Satnam Singh and Salman Khan win a bronze medal in the men’s double sculls in rowing. The men’s skeet shooting team comprising Anantjeet Singh Naruka, Bhavtegh Singh Gill and Mairaj Ahmad Khan won a bronze medal.

Manipur’s Roshibina Devi Naorem won silver in Wushu. This is her third straight Asian Games medal and second silver medal.

Indian men’s badminton team, led by Lakshya Sen, Ayush Shetty, Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, secured a bronze medal at the continental event, settling for third after losing 1-3 to China in the semifinals.

Jay Meena secured India’s first-ever soft tennis medal in Asian Games, clinching bronze after losing to Japan’s Takuya Kurosaka in the men’s singles semifinals.

Meanwhile, star Indian weightlifter Mirabai Chanu completed her Asian Games medal collection by winning the elusive silver in the women’s 49kg event.

India also secured its sixth shooting medal as the women’s skeet team, comprising Raiza Dhillon, Maheshwari Chauhan and Parinaaz Dhaliwal, won a bronze.

Earlier, the Indian Women’s 10 M Air Rifle team, comprising Elavenil Valarivan, Sonam Maskar, and Vidarsa Vinod, bagged a silver medal. Elavenil Valarivan also won another in Women’s 10 M Air Rifle Individual.

Rudrankksh Patil, Himanshu Dhillon, and Parth Mane won a silver in men’s 10 M Air Rifle team. Himanshu Dhillon also won a silver in Men’s 10 M Air Rifle Individual.

Two bronze medals were won by Rudranksh Patil in the Men’s 10 M Air Rifle Individual, and Suchika Tariyal in Women’s Traditional MMA 60 kg.

India won its first gold on September 22 with Harmanpreet Kaur-led team defeating Sri Lanka by 147 runs in the women’s cricket final. With the victory in Japan’s Aichi-Nagoya, India has successfully defended the title they won at the previous edition.

India is currently in 12th place on the medal table with 37 medals. China leads the table with 208 medals, which include 120 gold. Japan is in the second spot with 157 medals, followed by Republic of Korea which has secured 84 medals, including 21 gold.

A contingent of 501 Indian athletes, comprising 267 men and 234 women, is competing across 36 disciplines at the 2026 Asian Games. They aim to build on a historic performance at the Hangzhou Games, where India finished fourth behind China, Japan and South Korea with an impressive haul of 106 medals.

Also Read: Asian Games 2026: Deepika’s eight-goal blitz powers India to 19-0 hockey win over Uzbekistan

India’s campaign at this Quadrennial spectacle is led by some of the nation’s biggest sports icons, including Manu Bhaker, Mirabai Chanu, Lovlina Borgohain, P.V. Sindhu, Aman Sehrawat, Tajinderpal Singh Toor, Gulveer Singh, Harmanpreet Singh, Smriti Mandhana, and Jasprit Bumrah.
